title: When Will Rockies See Fortunes Change?
description: A long losing streak, when the team had been trying to move into fourth place in the National League West Division, doesn't bring good news to the Colorado Rockies.
fullText:
Before heading out on a road trip that started on Monday night with a 13-3 blowout loss to the Washington Nationals, the Colorado Rockies lost two three-game series at Coors Field.

That happened after Colorado had put together a few wins and appeared to have some momentum toward challenging the San Francisco Giants for fourth place in the National League West Division.

Now, though, that momentum has been dumped as the Rockies have now lost seven straight games. This is not what Rockies manager Warren Schaeffer probably wanted to see his team do entering the season's final weeks.

When looking at what is costing Colorado in the win column, it's not the hitting so much. There is offense being created thanks to Jake McCarthy, Ezequiel Tovar, Willi Castro, Hunter Goodman, and Mickey Moniak. Let's also not leave out what Cole Carrigg has done in his first number of games in the big leagues.

But, oh man, that pitching staff is not good. Tomoyuki Sugano has been the top pitcher throughout this season, but his ERA isn't too low. Sugano has a winning record and that does matter in the long run.

The Rockies' relievers have not been able to be consistent all season long. They have been less than stellar when coming out of the bullpen, sometimes taking a solid start by a starter and letting it run away.

Toss in the fact that the team doesn't want to have another 100-loss season this year. Right now, it is fair to say that the Rockies are going further toward that triple-digit number than away from it. Also, let's not forget that the Rockies' starters in the starting lineup go out and give it their best.

Goodman is the center of the power production for Colorado. The ballclub needs to look seriously at building around him next season. Moniak just recently signed a new deal to remain with the Rockies. He, too, needs to be in the mix of players surrounding Goodman in 2027.

That is, of course, if there is a 2027 MLB season and not a lockout.

Nevertheless, Rockies president of baseball operations Paul DePodesta and general manager Josh Byrnes probably have something in mind before next season. What type of ballclub do they want on the field? What are the expectations of wins vs. losses next season? Can they trust the pitching staff they have now, or are they going to tear that down and start over?

The biggest challenge ahead of the Rockies before this season ends? Avoid losing 100 games. They will need to start piling up more wins than losses to make sure that does not happen.

fullText:
Dream news: Fans give Angel Reese her flowers for historic outing vs. Sparks appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Angel Reese had herself a night on Monday, leading the Atlanta Dream past the Los Angeles Sparks, 78-71, at Crypto.com Arena with a historic performance.

Reese finished with 11 points, a career-high 26 rebounds, three assists, and three steals. She set the league record for most rebounds in a game and most rebounds in a single season. Reese surpassed Chamique Holdsclaw and A'ja Wilson, respectively, for the impressive feats.

She leads the WNBA in rebounds this season with 12.4 per game. She has 458 rebounds and counting. She was the rebounding queen last season with 12.6 boards per game.

RECORD-BREAKING NIGHT FOR ANGEL REESE 🚨

A new WNBA record for rebounds in a game 👏 pic.twitter.com/AxZ1PqZ6XT

Fans gave the 24-year-old forward her flowers for her latest milestone.

"26 rebounds in a single game is purely historic! Angel Reese owns the glass," said @lucky_voller.

"All that backlash on her. She's really showing us what she can do," added @jackson_da55761.

"She's just getting warmed up. The girl got a motor on her," wrote @trapmamba318.

"I feel like she's working towards (being the) best rebounder of all time," posted @zaireoneal.

"26 REBOUNDS! ANGEL REESE, YOU'RE UNREAL. History right there!" commented @RebeccaJoy211.

The three-time All-Star grabbed at least 20 rebounds in a game for the fifth time since entering the WNBA in 2024.

Her tenacity and competitiveness have made her a menace on the glass. Even at LSU, the 6-foot-3 Reese was almost impossible to keep off the paint.

She tallied her 27th double-double of the season, the most by any player.

The Dream outrebounded the Sparks, 48-32, including 15-7 on the offensive glass. Reese had eight offensive rebounds.

Atlanta notched its fourth straight win and improved to 25-13.

title: Steelers Get Harsh Assessment From NFL Insider 3 Weeks Before Regular Season
description: An NFL insider is a little worried about the Pittsburgh Steelers this season after visiting them during a training camp tour. The post Steelers Get Harsh Assessment From NFL Insider 3 Weeks Before Regular Season appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are less than three weeks away from opening the regular season at Acrisure Stadium against the Atlanta Falcons. But they might not be heading toward winning back-to-back AFC North titles.

Sports Illustrated NFL Insider Albert Breer toured a handful of training camps this summer, and he told Fox Sports radio host Colin Cowherd that the Steelers could unravel fast this season.

"I think the obvious one might be Pittsburgh because of the age and the roster, Breer said Monday on "The Herd." "The construction of the team makes a lot of sense. If you think about it, it's Aaron Rodgers, and at receiver you got [Michael] Pittman Jr. and [DK] Metcalf, and you got Rico Dowdle coming in at running back and Pat Freiermuth at tight end. On defense, it's like veterans at every level. Cameron Heyward, T.J. Watt up front, Patrick Queen at linebacker, Jalen Ramsey, DeShon Elliott, and Jamel Dean in the secondary, and they have complex schemes coming in.

"Mike McCarthy is going to want to do a lot; he's going to be able to leverage a lot out of Aaron Rodgers becuase he's got veteran teammates. On defense, you've got Patrick Graham from the New England tree there going to try to throw a lot of volume at other offenses, and he's got the group to do it. It's just when you have that amount of age on your roster, you're walking a narrow path. Will the team wear down over the course of the year? What will practice look like in October and November, and will there be any injuries?"

It's no secret that the Steelers have the oldest roster in the NFL on average. According to Bill Speros at Bookies.com, the Steelers' roster averages 27 years and 98 days, about 96 days older than the next-oldest team, the Los Angeles Rams.

Having the oldest roster isn't the worst thing since a lot of veterans can help win games early on. But again, can the veterans stay healthy throughout a full season?

The Steelers might not have enough of a blend of youth and veterans to get through a full season and compete well into the playoffs.

Even though Breer might not be high on the Steelers this season, he liked what he saw from one of Pittsburgh's biggest rivals, the Cleveland Browns, this summer.

"The other one [training camp] where the energy sort of surprised me a little bit, and I guess it's timely considering everything that happened today was Cleveland," Breer added. "If you want to talk about being caught off guard a little bit, I just sensed really good energy with the Browns, and again, that is despite everything that's happened the last three or four days. But it does feel like Todd Monken has been able to inject a different feel to this team."

The Browns did seem to have good energy around them until they named Deshaun Watson the starting quarterback on Monday. Now it feels like Cleveland might not be on track to have a great season at all.

Pittsburgh should have a good chance of beating the Browns twice this season, and the first matchup between the two teams will be on "Thursday Night Football" in Cleveland in Week 4.

title: A's Notes: Twins Take Opener; Langeliers, De Vries Injury Updates
description: The A's continued an odd season of losing the first game of a series at home with a loss to the Twins. Shea Langeliers remains in the early recovery stages, while top prospect Leo De Vries may be out for the season.
fullText:
The Minnesota Twins jumped out to a 1-0 lead just four batters into the game on a Josh Bell double, and they never looked back, ultimately defeating the Athletics 9-6 after a late rally by the home team.

The A's are no strangers to losing the first game of a series in Sacramento, with the loss on Monday night dropping them to 2-9 in such games. The only two wins the A's have mustered in such contests have been the home opener on April 3 against the Houston Astros and a June 15 win over the Pittsburgh Pirates.

Since June 16, the A's have gone just 15-45, which is the worst record in baseball in that span. The San Francisco Giants rank 29th in wins in this time period with 23.

Jeffrey Springs lasted 4⅔ innings, giving up seven hits, four earned runs, two walks, and three strikeouts. Springs also gave up his 30th home run of the season, which has him in a three-way tie for second-most in MLB this season. Aaron Nola leads the way with 31.

Both Henry Bolte (3-for-4) and Jeff McNeil (3-for-5) had big days at the plate, with Bolte scoring three times and McNeil driving home two and scoring once himself.

Zack Gelof entered the game with an 0-for-18 slump, and after starting the evening 0-for-3, he singled on a sharp liner in the bottom of the eighth and added an RBI double in the ninth as part of a four-run frame for the A's.

We posted an injury update for the whole list of A's players on the IL, and one commenter asked why some of the players had the "out for season" designation, and others, like Shea Langeliers, did not.

The press release stated that Langeliers has started a hitting and throwing progression following surgery on his right knee on July 28. That does not mean that he's necessarily close to a return, however.

"Baseball activity is a good sign," A's manager Mark Kotsay said before Monday's game. "Obviously he's not one of the guys on the [60-day IL]. I would never want to put out a statement that says 'he's going to make it back.'"

Essentially Kotsay is saying that he's active, but in the early stages of a recovery, so there is still a lot of work to do. Keeping him off the 60-day IL has kept his chances at returning this season alive, though to what degree is uncertain. The expectation has always seemed to be that any return would be a late-season one, so he won't be back imminently.

Last week we reported that Leo De Vries has landed on the IL, and that his status was uncertain. When we saw that he'd been in San Jose, California, we reached out to a team representative to ask if he'd been at Stanford Medical for an injury check-up, and they said an update would be coming.

On Monday, Martín Gallegos reported that De Vries "is dealing with a sore right shoulder and is currently in Arizona rehabbing. He is sidelined from throwing for four weeks."

That should effectively end his season, with the Double-A regular season wrapping up in three weeks, on September 13. To make matters interesting, the Triple-A regular season ends on September 20, with the postseason to follow.

We have not checked to see if a promotion for a few games to end the season would be an option for the organization to consider at this time, but we will look for an answer this week.

title: Swansea City Make Enquiry for Wrexham Defender Conor Coady
description: It has been reported that Swansea City are interested in a possible transfer for Wrexham AFC defender Conor Coady as the Championship club seeks to improve its defensive lineup before the summer transfer window closes.
fullText:
It has been reported that Swansea City are interested in a possible transfer for Wrexham AFC defender Conor Coady as the Championship club seeks to improve its defensive lineup before the summer transfer window closes.

The Football League World reports that Swansea have identified the experienced centre-back as a potential transfer target, as Coady's future at STōK Cae Ras grows increasingly uncertain. This 33-year-old has not been included in any of Wrexham's matchday squads this season since returning from his loan at Charlton Athletic.

Interest from Swansea followed upon a major injury blow to Cameron Burgess, which left Vitor Matos with a shortage of central defenders.

Ben Cabango and Stephen Welsh, signed in the summer, have taken part in Swansea's first Championship matches, but since Burgess is unavailable, the club now need to look for more experience and depth before the September 1 deadline. Coady's record makes him a reasonable choice.

The player had only moved from Leicester City to Wrexham in August 2025, accepting a two-year contract as part of a deal reportedly worth about £2 million.

Conor Coady moved to Charlton Athletic on loan in January 2026. During his time at The Valley, Coady made 12 appearances, scoring one goal and assisting once, and also showed his versatility by playing in the midfield.

This summer he went back to Wrexham but has still been left out of Parkinson's competitive teams, which may mean that a permanent transfer could happen.

Since Coady came to the club, Wrexham's defensive choices have also changed quite a bit. Callum Doyle, Dominic Hyam and Zak Vyner have all joined the squad, which has increased the competition for spots and made it much more difficult for Coady to get back into the starting eleven.

Coady would bring Championship and Premier League experience, providing Swansea with leadership and organising the defensive line. He is also at ease when he moves into the midfield and can distribute the ball from deep, traits that could make him a useful player for a team aiming to build attacks from the back.

Coady is entering the last year of his contract, and while he is not included in the matchday squads, a move might be a good opportunity to reignite his playing career and help Swansea remain an established Championship side.

At this stage, the reported approach is understood to be an enquiry rather than an agreed transfer, but with the deadline approaching, Coady's future could be one of the stories during the final days of the window.

title: Dan Quinn puts an end to Sonny Styles' nonsense
description: Commanders coach Dan Quinn broke down Detroit's long touchdown run. Guess what? It wasn't Sonny Styles' fault.
fullText:
With the advent of social media, people constantly try to be controversial. Some speak about things they don't know, just hoping to say something that will make them go viral. One of the strangest fixations in the NFL right now is fans of other teams watching Commanders rookie linebacker Sonny Styles and calling him a bust after 30 or fewer preseason snaps.

For one, most don't even know what they're talking about. Others just repeat the same tired talking points they read online the prior week. Last week, social media "film analysts" picked one Styles play to dissect. In Saturday's game, Detroit quarterback Joshua Dobbs scored on a 50-yard run.

Later that day, the same "analysts" were back at it, calling Styles a bust, blaming the touchdown on him.

Clearly, they didn't know what they were talking about. Surprise.

On the play, rookie edge rusher Joshua Josephs — who otherwise had a terrific performance — lost contain, allowing Dobbs to break free for the long run. There was another breakdown by a Washington defender on the play — it wasn't Styles.

In case you missed it, here's the play. Watch No. 48, Josephs.

JOSH DOBBS TO THE HOUSE!

Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Ac2ExcheNS

Had Josephs kept contain on this play, Dobbs is bottled up, and this doesn't end up being a big play, much less a touchdown.

It was a good teaching moment for Josephs that you can bet head coach Dan Quinn and defensive coordinator Daronte Jones coached him up afterward.

So, why blame Styles? He's apparently the new flavor of the month for the untrained social media analysts.

On Monday, Quinn put the nonsense to rest.

"A good zone read for him, and he's got that ability like [QB] Jayden [Daniels] to hand it off and pull it," Quinn said of Dobbs.

"So, on that particular one, on that option, they read the defensive end. So, if the defensive end closes, he pulls it. So, on that particular one, we'd love Josh [Josephs] to wait it out. And then we were in man-to-man behind, so once it's handed off and we're out of pass, get off your man, and everybody get back to it. So, I get it could be a first down, but to have it be a touchdown was certainly disappointing. But it would start with Josh, and then, just backside pursuit and speed to finish. But he made a good play, too."

It's time to put this one to bed.

title: Nottingham Forest vs Leeds United – Match preview and team news
description: Nottingham Forest and Leeds United meet for the second time in four days on Tuesday, with the Carabao Cup second round bringing them back to the City Ground so soon after Leeds won their Premier Leagu...
fullText:
Nottingham Forest and Leeds United meet for the second time in four days on Tuesday, with the Carabao Cup second round bringing them back to the City Ground so soon after Leeds won their Premier League curtain-raiser there 1-0.

Anton Stach's stoppage-time free-kick separated the sides on Saturday in what was Oliver Glasner's first competitive match in charge of Forest, despite his side creating the better chances across the 90 minutes. The rematch gives Glasner an immediate opportunity to put that result right, though he has already signalled there will be changes to his side.

Daniel Farke's Leeds arrive full of confidence after a strong pre-season and a composed win on the opening weekend, and the Yorkshire club will see this tie as a genuine chance to reach the third round of the Carabao Cup for the first time under their current manager. Both sides are expected to rotate significantly, with several summer signings from each club in line for their first taste of action together.

Date: Tuesday, 25 August 2026Kick-off: 20:00 BSTVenue: The City GroundReferee: Andrew KitchenLast meeting: Leeds United 1-0 Nottingham Forest, Premier League, 22 August 2026

Ryan Yates and Nicolo Savona remain sidelined through injury, and Morgan Gibbs-White will also miss out after picking up a knock in Saturday's defeat. Glasner confirmed there is no structural damage to Gibbs-White's knee but said "it doesn't make sense to play him" given the pain involved. The head coach has been open about wanting "fresh legs" for this tie, confirming "there will be moderate rotation" from the side beaten by Leeds.

Willy Gnonto and Gabriel Gudmundsson are both out with muscle injuries, Gnonto having picked his up in a pre-season friendly against Manchester United in Dublin. Ilia Gruev remains a long-term absentee with a knee issue, though he has partially reintegrated into training. New signing Nico Elvedi, cleared to play before the weekend but left out of the matchday XI, is expected to be given his first involvement in this tie.

Glasner's first competitive match in charge ended in defeat, but the performance offered encouragement, with Nikola Milenkovic and Igor Jesus both missing good first-half chances before Stach's late intervention settled it. The Austrian arrives with a strong pedigree in cup competitions, having won the Conference League, FA Cup and Community Shield during his time at Crystal Palace. Forest have also lost a key player this summer, with Elliot Anderson departing for Manchester City in a £116 million deal.

Farke's side head into the tie in good spirits, having beaten Forest through Stach's stunning late strike and enjoyed a productive pre-season that included wins over Sunderland, Liverpool and RB Leipzig. Leeds have become notably difficult to break down since switching to a back three under Farke in December, a shape they carried into the weekend's win. The manager will use Tuesday's tie to build depth and match fitness among several squad players.

Nottingham Forest predicted XI (3-4-2-1): John Victor; Diomande, Abbott, Murillo; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Netz; Kalimuendo, Hudson-Odoi; Wood

Leeds United predicted XI (3-4-3): Perri; Elvedi, Rodon, Muharemovic; Bogle, Tanaka, Longstaff, Justin; James, Nmecha, Okafor

The match will be broadcast live in the United Kingdom on ITV1, Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Football.

title: LASK vs Celtic – Match preview and team news
description: Celtic prepares to meet the Austrian side LASK in the second leg of their final UCL qualifying match on Tuesday away from home at the Raiffeisen Arena.LASK vs Celtic – Match preview and team newsDa...
fullText:
Celtic prepares to meet the Austrian side LASK in the second leg of their final UCL qualifying match on Tuesday away from home at the Raiffeisen Arena.

LASK Linz faces a monumental task to overturn their three-goal deficit but takes comfort in a highly stable squad situation ahead of the return leg at the Raiffeisen Arena.

Manager Dietmar Kuhbauer reported no fresh injury concerns following their physical first-leg encounter at Celtic Park, allowing him to field his strongest possible core.

The Austrian side's only major squad absence is forward Ramiz Harakaté, who remains completely sidelined for the foreseeable future due to an ACL tear.

Kuhbauer is widely expected to stick with his structured 3-5-2 system, utilizing a back three of Xavier Mbuyamba, Alemão, and Andrés Andrade to stifle Celtic's wingers.

However, team sources indicate LASK will adopt an aggressive tactical shift in the second half, bringing on extra attacking options if they need to chase quick goals.

Manager Martin O'Neill faces late selection headaches. Center-back Auston Trusty missed the final training session due to a stomach illness, meaning Liam Scales is on standby to anchor the defense alongside Cameron Carter-Vickers.

The Hoops are stretched thin at full-back, with regular right-back Alistair Johnston ruled out until October following a hamstring injury.

Colby Donovan is prepared to step up again in his place. In midfield and attack, Celtic must navigate the match without the suspended Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, while Portuguese winger Jota remains a long-term absentee as he continues his recovery from a severe cruciate ligament injury.

Viljami Sinisalo is tipped to start in goal, protected by a makeshift backline featuring Kieran Tierney.

LASK Linz enters this fixture in dominant domestic form, having won all four of their competitive domestic matches. In the Austrian Bundesliga, they cruised to three consecutive victories—beating Grazer AK 3-0, Austria Wien 2-0, and SV Ried 4-1—alongside a resounding 7-0 win in the Austrian Cup. However, their perfect start to the season was halted by a heavy 3-0 first-leg defeat against Celtic in Glasgow.

Celtic FC boasts a flawless start to their competitive campaign under Martin O'Neill, winning all four of their matches while scoring 13 goals and conceding just once. Their recent results include domestic wins over Dundee FC (1-0) and Kilmarnock (5-1) in the Premiership, a 4-0 thrashing of Dundee United in the League Cup, and a commanding 3-0 victory over LASK in their first-leg tie.

Celtic: Sinisalo; Donovan, Carter-Vickers, Scales, Tierney; Nygren, McGregor, Baur; Duran, Hogh, Hyun-Jun

Jack Rudoni's return gives Lampard fully available options in midfield alongside new signing Gustav Hamer, who rejoined the club permanently this summer. title: NY Rangers Could Have a Surprising Roster Cut Coming
description: The NY Rangers could end up with a relatively complex roster decision at training camp this fall, as surprising as it may be. The post NY Rangers Could Have a Surprising Roster Cut Coming appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The NY Rangers could be facing a rather surprising roster decision when training camp arrives later this fall.

That roster decision could lead to a once blue line mainstay on the outside looking in: Urho Vaakanainen.

That might seem implausible considering Vaakanainen is a perfectly capable NHL defenseman. But that's exactly what makes this situation somewhat complex. The Rangers have added more competition to their blue line, and suddenly there may not be enough room for everyone.

The NY Rangers brought in Marcus Pettersson and Sean Durzi, while players such as Matthew Robertson and Drew Fortescue are also competing for opportunities. Scott Morrow in particular is expected to challenge for a spot on the NHL roster.

Vaakanainen could ultimately be the unfortunate victim of it.

This isn't necessarily an indictment of his playing ability. It could simply be about the Rangers deciding that younger players need the opportunity to show what they can do. And that could leave Vaakanainen squeezed out of the lineup.

The problem for Vaakanainen is that he isn't exactly a stalwart for the NY Rangers

He's a reliable defensive option, but he isn't likely to provide the offensive upside of some of the Rangers' other options. He's also not the kind of physical presence that makes him indispensable in a depth role.

That makes him relatively easy to push down the depth chart. Petterson and Durzi have already done that.

Morrow, meanwhile, represents something the NY Rangers don't have nearly as much of with their veteran defensemen: Upside expectations.

If the Blueshirts believe Morrow can eventually become a legitimate top-four blueliner, giving him NHL minutes becomes much more valuable than continuing to give playing time to a 27-year-old depth player.

The same logic applies to Vincent Iorio. Yes, he's a good depth piece, but not quite the piece that would transform the NY Rangers' defense corps.

The Blueshirts don't need to know what Vaakanainen can become. They already have a pretty good idea.

They need to figure out what their younger defensemen can become. That's why Vaakanainen could be the odd man out despite being perfectly serviceable.

And there is another issue. If the Rangers decide they want to give one of their younger defensemen a permanent NHL opportunity, someone has to go. Vaakanainen is simply one of the easiest players to identify as the expendable piece.

It's harsh, but that's how roster construction works.

NY Rangers Biggest Need Is Also Most Obvious One

Of course, there is another possibility. Vaakanainen could remain with the team.

The NY Rangers might decide that having a reliable seventh or eighth defenseman is more important than forcing a younger player into the lineup before he's ready. That could leave Vaakanainen on the roster, but his role would probably be significantly diminished. Instead of being counted on for regular minutes, he could become the insurance policy.

That's actually a pretty valuable role over an 82-game season. Injuries happen, players struggle, meaning that someone eventually needs to step into the lineup. Having a defenseman who already knows how to play at the NHL level gives the Rangers some protection against those problems.

And if Vaakanainen is willing to accept that role, keeping him around makes sense.

The question is whether the NY Rangers believe the roster spot is better used on a younger player. That's what makes this situation worth watching. Vaakanainen isn't necessarily being pushed out because he's bad. He could be pushed out because the blueshirts have decided that the future is more important than squeezing a few more minutes out of a proven depth defenseman.

And if that's the decision the organization makes, it would be one of the more surprising roster cuts of training camp.

fullText:
Dodgers news: Blake Snell gets new company in extremely exclusive Rays club appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Blake Snell has been quite brilliant for the Los Angeles Dodgers ever since he came off the injured list. He's allowed just two earned runs in 18.0 innings pitched since, lowering his ERA to 2.57 on the season. Snell continues to be one of the best pitchers in MLB, as he has been since the start of his big-league career with the Tampa Bay Rays.

The Rays traded Snell back in 2020, with Tampa Bay selling high on him even though he was still under contract until the end of the 2023 season. This is Tampa Bay's standard operating procedure; they keep the line moving to avoid running into payroll problems as a small-market club.

Since then, the Rays have developed quite a few quality starting pitchers. In 2026, one of their best starters has been Drew Rasmussen, who pitched another quality start for Tampa Bay in a 4-1 win over the Detroit Tigers on Monday. Rasmussen earned the win after he allowed just one earned run on three hits in six innings of work, striking out five while walking none.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

With that latest win for Rasmussen, he became just the second pitcher in Rays history to earn a win in at least seven consecutive starts, joining Blake Snell in that exclusive club, according to MLB Stats on X.

Snell accomplished the feat in 2018, when he earned a win in nine consecutive starts for the Rays. During that nine-game stretch, Snell pitched 52.2 innings and allowed just six earned runs, which was good for an ERA of 1.03. He ended that season with a win-loss record of 21-5.

Even though the Rays finished 2018 with a 90-72 record, they missed the postseason after finishing third in the stacked AL East.

In 2026, the Rays have led the AL East for much of the season and are currently on top of the division with a 78-53 record. Rasmussen has a 14-5 record this year with an ERA of 2.95 across 140.1 innings (25 starts).

title: Liverpool have already signed their Virgil van Dijk replacement and it isn't Jacquet
description: Liverpool already have their Virgil van Dijk replacement. What a colossus Van Dijk has been over the years for the Reds. There will likely never be a player like him.The Dutchman has been one of the d...
fullText:
Liverpool already have their Virgil van Dijk replacement.

What a colossus Van Dijk has been over the years for the Reds. There will likely never be a player like him.

The Dutchman has been one of the defining players of the club's modern era, transforming the defence after his arrival and becoming a leader both on and off the pitch. His presence has given Liverpool something every top team needs a defender that is unbeatable.

At his best, Van Dijk makes defending look remarkably simple. His positioning, reading of the game and ability to win duels allow him to deal with dangerous situations before they even become problems. He also has the pace and physicality to recover when things go wrong, while his passing ability allows Liverpool to build attacks from the back.

But perhaps his biggest value comes from his leadership.

Van Dijk has worn the captain's armband through some of Liverpool's most important moments and has become a calm, authoritative figure in the dressing room. That experience is particularly important when younger defenders are still finding their feet.

Liverpool can replace a centre-back statistically. Replacing Van Dijk's influence is far more difficult.

With the club undergoing another period of transition, his experience could prove crucial. He provides stability in a defence that has faced plenty of change, while his standards continue to set the benchmark for those around him.

For Liverpool, Van Dijk remains much more than just another defender.

If the Dutchman eventually leaves Liverpool, one of the biggest questions will be who takes over the captaincy.

Andoni Iraola has already named three vice-captains in Joe Gomez, Alisson Becker and Dominik Szoboszlai, which would appear to put those three at the front of the queue. However, there is an obvious complication.

Both Gomez and Alisson are entering the final year of their contracts just like Van Dijk, meaning their futures beyond next summer remain uncertain. If either leaves, Liverpool could quickly find themselves looking elsewhere for their next leader.

So, it's quite obvious what the plan is in terms of replacing Van Dijk as the club's captain.

Liverpool have already signed him - Dominik Szoboszlai.

The Hungarian has already established himself as an important figure within the squad and his influence has continued to grow. He also has the advantage of being tied down to a long-term contract.

Beyond those three, Liverpool could eventually look towards players such as Alexis Mac Allister or Ryan Gravenberch, depending on how their roles develop.

But Szoboszlai is by far and away the most logical successor. He is the one who stepped up at St James' Park to deliver an equaliser and he has a lot of experience leading his country at international level.

Speaking to reporters after the Newcastle game as per The Independent, Van Dijk backed the Hungarian to succeed him.

"Every leadership group is important. Obviously there is experience and there is someone in terms of Dom who has been the captain of his country, and that will only help him to be part of this group," Van Dijk said.

"He has to take responsibility to take that on his shoulders and it is going to benefit us also in the long run with Szoboszlai signing a new deal. He will be here to take over."

With the current captain backing him to do so, it's quite obvious that the Reds already know how this is going to go.

Their Van Dijk replacement is already primed and ready to go in Szoboszlai.

title: Sparks lose to Dream as Reese sets record for most rebounds in WNBA game
description: LOS ANGELES -- This was a much better contest than the one on Thursday.
fullText:
LOS ANGELES -- This was a much better contest than the one on Thursday.

Unfortunately for the Sparks, the result was the same.

Angel Reese seemed to grab the ball every time it was in the air. She would end the game with a record 26 rebounds and the Dream defeated the Sparks in a hard-fought match, 78-71.

The Sparks only outrebounded Reese by herself, 32-26, which sounds ridiculous.

"She's elite," Sparks coach Lynne Roberts said about Reese. "Did we miss her a couple times on the boards? Eight offensive rebounds is a ton. But I think she's the best in the world at it. I really do. I think she has a way of... her timing is good, she's strong, she's got great physicality, but she knows how to kind of lean to kind of get you out of position to where you can now jump and do it. She does a good job tipping it kind of to herself. She's good. Could we have done a better job? Certainly. But you also have to tip your hat to who I think is one of the best rebounders in the world."

Nneka Ogwumike did have an outstanding game herself. A vintage performance as some might say.

"It feels like a blessing," Ogwumike said about retiring at the top of her game. "I've always been kind of the type of player that said that I didn't want to get dragged off the court. But I do feel like what I do have left I'm pouring into these last few games and I'm grateful to be doing it in this uniform. And also to be, you know, being able to hopefully impact some of my teammates, most especially (Cameron Brink) here. We have a very unique and very special sisterly bond. However, I can imprint some level of inspiration for her and my teammates on my way out is really what I want to do."

"Like Nneka said, we have such a great bond," Brink said. "I think I look to her for a lot of strength and she's so amazing at encouraging me. There was a couple plays where I wanted her to be the one to set a down screen for the post-up look and she was like, 'no, you go.' And I was like, 'oh, sure, man.' And so I feel like I get really emotional thinking that I'm not going to have that next year with you. But I do know I'm going to always be able to call on you for that. So it's not just Nneka; it's everybody. But I think just leaning on my people has been really important."

As for the Dream (25-13), they were able to get out of the first half deficit and go on an 18-6 run that started with Naz Hillmon's three before the end of the second quarter. The Dream did not relinquish the lead after that.

"I think we were missing shots. And that got them out playing a little looser," Roberts said. "It's a really good team. And they regrouped at halftime and came out and kind of punched us there in the third. And I will say there was a moment there where these guys could have packed it in or just kind of gone through the motions and they didn't. And we have not all season long. And I do think that's a credit to Nneka, to the leaders of this group, that they're not going to let that happen. So, yeah, they're a good team, right? And they came out a little more organized there in the third. And we just didn't have a great shooting night if you look at the percentages.

"But I thought our process was good, what we were trying to do on offense," Roberts continued. "The ball was trying to be moved. They were looking for each other. Sometimes, it just doesn't bounce your way."

Neither team had a great shooting night: Dream shot .400 while the Sparks went .388 from the field. It's the three-point shooting that betrayed the Sparks once again: they went 3 for 18 (.167) while Atlanta wasn't much better at 6 for 29 (.207). But it was Angel Reese's work on the glass that dominated the game.

Reese also scored 11 points to get her 27th double-double of the season. That's one short of tying the record set by Alyssa Thomas for most double-doubles (28) in a season. Allisha Gray led the Dream in scoring with 20 points.

That vintage performance by Ogwumike went for 27 points and 16 rebounds. Dearica Hamby and Brink each scored 15 points. Brink also tied her career-high with five blocks. Los Angeles was without Rae Burrell, who missed her first game of the season due to an illness.

The Sparks (13-25) have one more game in their home stand as they take on the Washington Mystics on Friday. After that, they'll have one more game on the road (in Seattle) before they take their World Cup break for the next two and a half weeks.

The New York Jets actually look like they have some genuine momentum. After dropping their preseason opener to Tampa Bay, Aaron Glenn's team responded with a statement performance in Pittsburgh. Suddenly, the competition for roster spots feels considerably more consequential. Geno Smith has already demonstrated that the offense can operate efficiently under Frank Reich. There defense has generated pressure and turnovers. With one preseason game remaining against the Giants, the Jets must separate legitimate contributors from temporary summer standouts. This will determine which 53 players give them the best chance to compete when the games finally count.

The Jets sit at 1-1 through two preseason games. They recovered from a 24-16 home defeat against Tampa Bay with a dominant 17-0 shutout of Pittsburgh at Acrisure Stadium. The encouraging response has given Glenn's revamped squad some much-needed confidence. Smith was particularly impressive in his preseason debut. He completed all seven of his passes on a touchdown drive while operating Reich's offense with efficiency and rhythm. Meanwhile, the defense overwhelmed Pittsburgh with four sacks and two takeaways. That offered a glimpse of the aggressive identity Glenn wants to establish. The Giants now provide the final measuring stick before New York must finalize its 53-man roster.

Quarterback (2): Geno Smith, Cade Klubnik

Smith has the experience and accuracy to serve as the unquestioned starter. His early preseason performance reinforced why the Jets believe he can provide stability. Reich's system should allow Smith to operate from structure while taking advantage of his ability to make quick decisions. Klubnik earns the backup spot. He gives New York a developmental option with enough mobility to expand the offense when necessary. The Jets ultimately cannot afford to devote a third roster spot to the position.

Running Back (5): Breece Hall, Braelon Allen, Isaiah Davis, Kene Nwangwu, Andrew Beck

Hall remains the centerpiece because of his home-run potential. The Jets have every reason to maximize his touches. Allen provides physicality and complementary early-down work. Davis gives the team another capable runner. Nwangwu's value extends beyond the backfield because of his special-teams ability. Beck's fullback versatility makes him particularly useful in short-yardage packages. It is an unusually deep group, but every member offers a distinct role.

Wide Receiver (6): Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, Omar Cooper Jr, Tim Patrick, Arian Smith, Isaiah Williams

Wilson should remain the primary target in Reich's passing attack. His ability to win at multiple levels gives Smith a reliable option. Mitchell brings size and vertical ability. Patrick supplies veteran experience and contested-catch reliability. Cooper and Arian Smith add explosiveness. Williams provides versatility from multiple alignments.

Tight End (3): Mason Taylor, Kenyon Sadiq, Jelani Woods

Taylor projects as an important receiving component. Sadiq adds athleticism and the ability to threaten defenses vertically. Woods provides a massive target and a useful option in the red zone.

Offensive Line (9): Olu Fashanu, Dylan Parham, Josh Myers, Joe Tippmann, Armand Membou, Max Mitchell, Chukwuma Okorafor, Xavier Newman, Anez Cooper

Fashanu anchors the left side. Membou handles the right tackle position. Myers gives the interior a veteran presence at center. Parham and Tippmann complete the projected starting configuration. The depth is arguably just as important. Mitchell's ability to play multiple positions, Okorafor's tackle experience, and Newman's interior versatility provide insurance against potential injuries.

Defensive line (5): T'Vondre Sweat, Harrison Phillips, David Onyemata, Jowon Briggs, Darrell Jackson Jr

Sweat and Phillips provide substantial size and power. Onyemata adds veteran savvy and pass-rushing experience. Briggs offers rotational flexibility, with Jackson providing additional depth. The objective is clear: force opposing offenses to account for the interior before they can attack the Jets' edge rushers.

EDGE (5): David Bailey, Will McDonald IV, Joseph Ossai, Kingsley Enagbare, Nate Lynn

McDonald is the explosive pass-rushing threat capable of changing games. Bailey and Ossai provide additional pressure packages. Enagbare brings versatility and experience, and Lynn rounds out the rotation.

Linebacker (4): Demario Davis, Jamien Sherwood, Francisco "Kiko" Mauigoa, Marcelino McCrary-Ball

Davis supplies the veteran leadership and football intelligence. Sherwood complements him with athleticism and range. Mauigoa and McCrary-Ball provide younger rotational options. The Jets do not need this group to dominate statistically if the defensive line and secondary can consistently create favorable situations.

Cornerback (6): Brandon Stephens, Nahshon Wright, Jarvis Brownlee Jr, Azareye'h Thomas, D'Angelo Ponds, Qwan'tez Stiggers

Stephens provides experience on the perimeter. Wright adds another lengthy coverage option. Brownlee and Thomas give the Jets additional physicality. Ponds and Stiggers provide depth and developmental upside.

Safety (5): Minkah Fitzpatrick, Andre Cisco, Dane Belton, Malachi Moore, Samuel Womack III

Fitzpatrick gives Glenn the freedom to move him around the formation. Cisco brings playmaking ability. Belton, Moore, and Womack provide rotational and special-teams value.

Kicker: Jason Sanders
Punter: Austin McNamara
Long Snapper: Thomas Hennessy.

Sanders gives the Jets a proven option at kicker. McNamara handles punting and holding duties. Hennessy provides continuity at long snapper. With the rest of the roster undergoing significant transition, maintaining stability here is particularly valuable.

The Jets' projected roster reflects a team attempting to establish a completely different identity. Smith and Hall provide recognizable offensive pillars. Wilson gives the passing game a legitimate focal point. The combination of Fitzpatrick, Davis, and an aggressive front gives Glenn the ingredients for a physical defense.

The biggest question is whether the depth chart can translate the optimism of August into sustained regular-season performance. For a Jets organization attempting to turn encouraging flashes into meaningful progress, the final 53-man roster may be the first real blueprint of what this new era intends to become.

title: Canucks Should Consider Surprising Choice for Next Captain
description: With the Vancouver Canucks going through a transition period, it might not be the craziest idea to make a surprising choice for team captain. The post Canucks Should Consider Surprising Choice for Next Captain appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Vancouver Canucks have spent much of the offseason looking like a team trying to find a new identity.

The club lost much of it when Quinn Hughes departed. And with the roster getting younger, the organization is essentially accumulating assets. That situation means Canucks fans could be staring at a much longer rebuild than they realize.

And yet, there's one rather important player who hasn't gone anywhere.

Elias Pettersson. Yes, that's right.

For all the speculation surrounding his future in Vancouver, there has been no indication that the Canucks have actually approached Pettersson about waiving his no-movement clause. That's an important distinction.

A lot of the conversation has centered on what Vancouver could do with Pettersson.

But what if the organization doesn't actually want to trade him?

Pettersson is one of the longest-tenured players on the roster and one of its most experienced. If the Canucks genuinely believe he's going to remain part of the organization through this rebuild, perhaps they should give him a different responsibility.

Perhaps he should be the next captain.

There's no question Pettersson has struggled to live up to expectations in recent seasons. That's precisely why this idea is a little unconventional.

The Canucks don't necessarily need Pettersson to become the 100-point superstar he once appeared destined to be. If that version of him returns, fantastic. But perhaps his most important contribution to this team won't come from scoring 100 points.

Pettersson has been through almost everything with the Canucks. He's experienced the highs, the lows, the playoff disappointment and the pressure that comes with being one of the organization's highest-paid players.

That's valuable experience for a rebuilding team.

If Vancouver isn't actually trying to move him, why not lean into that? Giving Pettersson the captaincy wouldn't magically solve his production problems. It wouldn't make the Canucks contenders overnight. But it would give him an opportunity to contribute in a way that doesn't involve carrying the offense every night.

And perhaps that would be good for everyone.

Instead of constantly wondering whether Pettersson is going to rediscover his old form, Vancouver could ask him to become one of the players responsible for helping establish the culture of the next Canucks team, even if Pettersson has become the poster child for everything that went wrong before the rebuild.

Canucks Will Need to Retain This Much to Trade Pettersson

The Canucks are going to have plenty of uncertainty over the next few years.

That's what happens during a rebuild. The last thing Vancouver needs is to simply drift aimlessly through that process. That's why having some semblance of stability could be incredibly important.

He's familiar with the organization, the city and the expectations that come with playing for the Canucks. More importantly, he has a long-term contract and, based on everything known, hasn't been asked to waive the protection that gives him control over his future.

If the organization views him as part of the rebuild, it should act like it.

Making Pettersson captain would send a pretty clear message. The Canucks aren't simply waiting for their next generation of stars to arrive. They're asking the players who have already been through the difficult years to help build the foundation around them.

Maybe Pettersson isn't the captain everyone expected.

But if Vancouver is stuck with him, and apparently, it isn't actually trying to get unstuck, why not give him a chance to become something more important than just another player on the roster?

title: Seattle Mariners Bats Come Alive in 9-2 Win Against Philadelphia Phillies
description: The Mariners handed Phillies starter Zack Wheeler his worst outing of the season and Cal Raleigh had a career-best night.
fullText:
Seattle Mariners manager Dan Wilson speaks to the media following the team's 9-2 win against the Philadelphia Phillies on Monday at T-Mobile Park in Seattle. | Teren Kowatsch

SEATTLE — Any concerns about whether or not the Seattle Mariners would have a lingering hangover following their 19-2 loss against the Chicago Cubs on Sunday were quickly answered in the M's game against the Philadelphia Phillies on Monday at T-Mobile Park.

The Mariners beat the Phillies 9-2 off the back of a five-run, two-homer first-inning. The Mariners need one more win in the final two games against the visitors to give themselves two consecutive series wins against National League teams in the playoff picture.

"You forget about (losses) quickly and move on," Seattle manager Dan Wilson said in a postgame interview Monday. "These guys have been able to do it. And I think we've been tested a little bit this last week with the one-sided games. ... Each time, they've come out the next day and really gotten out on the board and ahead of the other club and put up some runs early."

Before the Mariners' bats came alive in the bottom of the first, the team started out with a marginal deficit.

In the top of the first inning, Seattle starting pitcher Logan Gilbert issued a lead-off walk to Phillies designated hitter Kyle Schwarber. After striking out shortstop Trea Turner, back-to-back singles from right fielder Bryce Harper and second baseman Luis Arraez gave the visitors the bases loaded with no outs.

Philadelphia only got one out of the situation after first baseman Alec Bohm grounded into a fielder's choice (which brought home Schwarber and gave the Phillies a 1-0 lead) and Gilbert struck out third baseman Bryson Stott.

Gilbert threw 29 pitches in the first inning, but powered through and finished his outing with five strikeouts, two walks and two earned runs allowed on five hits (one homer) in five innings pitched.

Gilbert was able to outduel visiting starter Zack Wheeler, who had arguably his worst outing of the season Monday. Wheeler fanned four, walked five, threw a wild pitch and allowed eight earned runs on nine hits (four homers) in four innings pitched.

"Last game, this game, (the offense) has been helping me out a lot," Gilbert said after the game. "I appreciate it. Going against an arm like (Wheeler), that's one of the best for years when he's on. That's hard to do."

The Mariners immediately responded in the bottom of the first. Left fielder Randy Arozarena hit a lead-off walk and right fielder Dominic Canzone hit a single to set center fielder Julio Rodriguez up for a three-run homer.

Rodriguez's multi-run shot was his 20th home run of the season, which made him the first player in Seattle history to begin his career with five-straight years with 20 or more homers.

frozen rope to left 🥶 pic.twitter.com/LHNRlYnSFV

Three batters later, after designated hitter Taylor Ward drew a one-out walk, Cal Raleigh joined the home run part with a two-run shot to right field to bolster the Mariners' lead to 5-1.

That homer was the first of three on the night for Raleigh, the first time he's achieved that feat in his career.

Raleigh's second homer was a solo shot in the bottom of the fifth and his third was another solo homer in the bottom of the seventh, the last of which resulted in the eventual final of 9-2.

Raleigh finished the game 3-for-3 with three runs, three homers and four RBIs.

"I think it's just having that belief," Raleigh said in a postgame interview. "You're always fine-tuning your swing, stuff like that. But at the same time, just (have) that belief in yourself and trust in what you do. Just execute when you get that pitch. ... I'm feeling better in the box. I feel like I've been seeing the ball pretty well."

ohhh baby a THREE HOMER GAME!! pic.twitter.com/R2ffx1qkW5

The only other blemish for Seattle was a solo homer surrendered to Philadelphia catcher J.T. Realmuto in the top of the second.

The Mariners continued to build their advantage after Raleigh's first homer. Rodriguez scored on a wild pitch in the bottom of the third to make the lead 6-2 and second baseman Cole Young hit a solo homer after Raleigh's second blast in the bottom of the fifth to bolster the team's lead to 8-2.

Cole wanted in on the dinger party 🎉 pic.twitter.com/JKcGgzqcZ0

After Gilbert's exit, the bullpen shut down the Phillies offense. The trio of Seranthony Dominguez, Gabe Speier and Carlos Vargas combined for three strikeouts in four innings of work and didn't allow a hit or a free base. Dominguez pitched two inning and fanned two.

Seattle will try and clinch the series win in game two against Philadelphia at 6:40 p.m. PT on Tuesday at T-Mobile Park. George Kirby will start for the Mariners and Aaron Nola will start for the Phillies.

title: Chelsea plotting move for Atalanta’s Honest Ahanor
description: Chelsea are keeping tabs on Atalanta defender Honest Ahanor, according to Fabrizio Romano.The Blues are eyeing the 18-year-old as one for the future, and it remains unclear how willing they are to bri...
fullText:
Chelsea are keeping tabs on Atalanta defender Honest Ahanor, according to Fabrizio Romano.

The Blues are eyeing the 18-year-old as one for the future, and it remains unclear how willing they are to bring him to Stamford Bridge.

The Chelsea target caught the eye in Serie A playing as a centre-half and a left-wing-back.

Ahanor won 55 percent of his aerial and 62% of his ground duels last season while helping to keep four clean sheets in 22 league appearances.

Interestingly, the Italian club has already rejected two offers for his services, and it remains to be seen whether Chelsea can convince them to part ways.

He 'has been touted as a potential star for some time now.' There was a reason Atalanta paid €16 million plus €4m in bonuses around this time last year for his services.

Ahanor, who represents Italy at youth levels but is eligible to play for Nigeria through both parents, has continued to impress, attracting attention from big clubs like Chelsea.

Chelsea and BlueCo already have enough young defenders on their books who need a clear pathway to first-team football.

Aaron Anselmino and Mamadou Sarr are both looking to develop away from Stamford Bridge.

Meanwhile, Josh Acheampong has already shown enough potential to deserve continued opportunities with the senior side.

There is little point adding another teenage defender to an already crowded group and then figuring out where he fits.

Chelsea's obsession with stockpiling young talent can become counterproductive when players are moved around or blocked from progressing naturally.

Ahanor may well develop into an excellent defender, but Chelsea do not need to sign every promising teenager who emerges.

They need to give the players they already have a genuine chance to establish themselves, as seen with Deivid Washington, David Datro Fofana, Mathis Amougou, etc.

Ahanor should be left right where he is and allowed to develop without Chelsea constantly tampering with his budding career.

title: Manchester City have made a call that may not be popular but could be the right one
description: The future of Nico Gonzalez at Manchester City became painstakingly clear on Sunday. Marc Guehi started in midfield and the Spanish midfielder was an unused substitute in City’s 2-1 win over Bournem...
fullText:
The future of Nico Gonzalez at Manchester City became painstakingly clear on Sunday. Marc Guehi started in midfield and the Spanish midfielder was an unused substitute in City's 2-1 win over Bournemouth. The fact that Guehi was preferred in midfield to Nico Gonzalez said all you needed to know about where he stands in Enzo Maresca's squad. It has been reported that Nico Gonzalez is set to sign for Newcastle United. That move may not be popular, but it may be for the best for Nico and Manchester City.

Nico Gonzalez is set to complete a permanent move to Newcastle United. Fabrizio Romano reports that Manchester City and Newcastle have agreed on a £50 million package that will see the Spanish midfielder depart the FA Cup and Carabao Cup holders. It is reported that Newcastle will pay £47 million plus £3 million in add-ons. Romano also reports that Nico will be a key player for Newcastle as they bid to replace Bruno Guimarães and Sandro Tonali.

During his time at Manchester City, Nico Gonzalez didn't really put a foot wrong. He was signed during the January 2025 transfer window when Pep Guardiola's squad was in desperate need of midfield reinforcement. He showed glimpses during the back end of that season that he could grow and become a consistent contributor for Pep Guardiola's side. He did play really well in the Rodri role during the first half of last season. However, when Rodri returned from injury, Nico's opportunities to play dried up.

During the closing stages of last season, Nico Gonzalez was left out of Manchester City's matchday squad altogether. It was thought that with Enzo Maresca coming in the equation could change for Nico. But it has not. Instead, he is on the verge of signing for Newcastle. Also, if Nico had come on as expected, perhaps Manchester City would not have been so eager to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille.

In the end, perhaps it is the right move for Manchester City to sell Nico Gonzalez to Newcastle. The Spanish midfielder should be an important player for them and he will get the opportunity to play regularly which wasn't going to arrive at City. That is probably the best move for all concerned despite it being an unpopular move.

title: Sunderland want Barcelona midfielder as Hansi Flick’s decision pushes exit closer
description: Marc Casado’s time at Barcelona appears to be moving towards its final chapter, with Sunderland now emerging as a serious contender for the midfielder’s signature.The 22-year-old has found himself...
fullText:
Marc Casado's time at Barcelona appears to be moving towards its final chapter, with Sunderland now emerging as a serious contender for the midfielder's signature.

The 22-year-old has found himself on the outside of Hansi Flick's plans, and the signs around his future have become difficult to ignore.

As reported before, Casado has been training separately from the main group for weeks as Barcelona and his representatives look for a solution before the transfer window closes.

Now, according to Mundo Deportivo, Sunderland have joined the growing list of Premier League clubs monitoring the Barcelona academy graduate.

The English side is understood to be in discussions over a potential move, giving Casado a possible route to remain in European football.

Barcelona are open to selling Casado. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

The Marc Casado transfer situation has been developing for some time.

With competition for places in Barcelona's midfield fierce, the Spaniard has been informed that regular opportunities will be difficult to come by under Flick.

His agent, Jorge Mendes, is therefore working on possible destinations. Casado has attracted offers from Saudi Arabia, but his preference is to stay in Europe and continue his career at a high level.

That decision has naturally opened the door to the Premier League.

On that note, Nottingham Forest had previously appeared to be among the strongest candidates for the Barcelona midfielder, while Aston Villa, Newcastle United and Brighton have also been linked with his situation.

Sunderland are interested in Marc Casado. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

As per the outlet, Sunderland are now negotiating Casado's arrival as they look to strengthen their midfield options.

The exact structure of a potential deal remains unclear, but Barcelona are believed to value the 22-year-old at between €30 million and €40 million.

From Barcelona's perspective, a successful sale would create room to continue shaping the squad.

Furthermore, the club could use the funds to pursue further signings and make final adjustments before the season develops further.

title: Why Ollie Watkins’ move to Saudi Arabia will tarnish his Aston Villa legacy
description: IN-DEPTH: The England striker seems dead set on leaving Villa in the lurch to join Al Hilal – which, Richard Jolly writes, is a great shame for a club and player who were very good for one another
fullText:
Where Unai Emery is concerned, the silent treatment has taken on a new meaning. The Aston Villa manager's pre-match interview at Brighton on Sunday was notable for a one-word answer. "Silence," he said, when asked about Ollie Watkins' whereabouts. The England striker was absent for the 4-0 defeat, Emery hinting he refused to play.

Watkins appears set on joining Al Hilal. A considerable boost to his bank balance would come with a dent to his reputation. For the nice guy, one of football's feel-good stories, it surely wasn't supposed to end like this. When Watkins was playing for Exeter at 21, the riches now offered in Saudi Arabia would have seemed unimaginable. But so, too, would have scoring the winner for England in the semi-final of a major tournament or winning a European trophy. This will be his last big contract – and presumably, much his biggest – but it again invites the question of how much money footballers need.

Six years at Villa Park should not have left him a pauper. Instead, he may leave Villa with Emi Buendia acting as a false nine at Brighton as they made a false start to their campaign.

A tarnished legacy would be a shame because Watkins and Villa have been very good for each other. He had never played in the top flight before he became their club record signing. He became the only player to reach double figures of Premier League goals in each of the last six seasons. His departure may be drawn out, but perhaps Watkins finished in a way with a match-winning brace against Manchester City, his last game at Villa Park, like his third, an evisceration of Liverpool. There were six goals in his last five games for Villa and, in the one where he did not find the net, they won the Europa League.

Watkins etched his name into Villa history; indeed he did so early on with his hat-trick in the 7-2 demolition of Liverpool in 2020. He became the first player since Peter McParland in 1962 to bring up a century of goals for them. That six-decade wait feels all the more astonishing given some of the calibre of players in the intervening period: Brian Little and Andy Gray, Peter Withe and Gary Shaw, David Platt and Dwight Yorke, Dion Dublin and Gabby Agbonlahor.

And yet there have been hints a relationship was frayed and fracturing. Another day when Watkins felt rampant came with the revelation he was angry: he destroyed Newcastle in April 2025 but, in his words, was "fuming" he had been confined to a brief outing in the Champions League quarter-final against Paris Saint-Germain, when Marcus Rashford was preferred. Yet by going now, he would deny himself a chance he wanted then and a role in just Villa's second European Cup campaign since 1983.

He was of interest to Arsenal in January 2025 and then Manchester United the following summer, suggesting either or both of a capacity to earn admirers with his performances or an active agent.

Now the timing of Watkins' wanderlust risks plunging Villa into decline. Perhaps the last week has been a tipping point in a summer that always promised some change. Villa may be stripped of six of the Europa League final starting 11.

Examine them and each case is different. For a club who have breached financial regulations, Morgan Rogers was always the likeliest candidate to command a sizeable fee and Villa got a huge one, in £117m. Youri Tielemans had a release clause, but still produced a £35m profit. Lucas Digne's departure had seemed an annual possibility and finally happened. Villa tired of Emi Martinez and signed a replacement, Zion Suzuki, before the goalkeeper had even gone.

But Villa surely did not bank on two others jumping ship. Ezri Konsa represents a fine price, with £51m for a defender who is almost 29. Like Watkins, though, he was a stalwart, a graduate of the lower leagues who became part of the core Emery inherited, this group signed by either Steve Bruce, Dean Smith or Steven Gerrard who were the constants amid the frantic trading.

John McGinn and Tyrone Mings could feel lonely, as the last survivors of that group, if the exodus continues. The purpose of the senior professionals has seemed to underpin the Emery era, helping them to recover from the tougher spells. Now that collective will be no more.

And if, in reality, Villa needed to get younger, suddenly they are being stripped of the certainties experience provided; in Watkins' case, that included a guarantee of goals, with at least 16 in each of the last three Premier League campaigns. Brian Madjo's superb Super Cup performance against PSG offered hope for a future beyond him but Tammy Abraham's ineffectual 2026 is a reminder Emery's recruitment at Villa has been decidedly mixed.

It is one cause for concern if Watkins is going. But even before then, it is the way he seems to be going.

title: The X factors that make Chantelle Cameron vs Mikaela Mayer must-watch boxing
description: Comment: Saturday’s main event may crown the sport’s top female star, just a fortnight before Katie Taylor retires
fullText:
Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron were part of a long list of women waiting for Katie Taylor to call, but the call never came. It was not a shock when they were both ignored ahead of Taylor's retirement party – in front of 80,000 at Croke Park in two weeks – but a fight between Mayer and Cameron themselves was a nice idea.

This Saturday, in Birmingham, they fight each other with three world-title belts on the line, and it is one of the very best fights that could be made in the women's game. It is an MVP promotion, their second in the UK, and once again the full card is exceptional. This time, American stars face Britain's own in every bout.

Mayer holds the WBC and WBA belts at super-welterweight, and Cameron has the WBO version, which means there will be a decent scuffle at the end between the commissioners in the ring, all desperate to attach their bauble to the champion first.

In an ideal boxing world, Cameron would be getting her third fight with Taylor, and Mayer (who first fought for a world title at super-feather, a full 24lb below this weekend's limit) would be fighting at a lighter weight.

The women's game often throws up odd fights at strange weights, and this is certainly one of the very best ever in that category. The willingness and ability of the top fighters to flip in and out of alien divisions has made the women's side of the sport so competitive.

American Mayer and Britain's Cameron are both senior members of the team, exceptional fighters, veterans of long and successful amateur careers, and have been in close to 25 world-title fights in five divisions as professionals. They have taken risks, taken hard fights on the road, and are now firmly established as two of the very best in their sport.

Cameron held a version of the world title at lightweight nine years ago, which is nearly 20lb below the super-welterweight limit. It can often feel like there are three weight classes: those under super-feather, then somewhere near the super-welterweight limit, then those up at middleweight and above. Small, medium, and big, if you like.

Mayer has lost just twice, both tight decisions and both in Britain; Cameron's only loss was in the rematch with Taylor in Dublin in 2023. They could, once Taylor retires at midnight in two weeks, be fighting for the unofficial crown of the world's top female boxer. Mayer against Cameron feels that big.

Caroline Dubois defends her two lightweight world championships on the same bill and is a contender for that same honorary title.

On Saturday night, there will be no time for getting a sense of distance, feeling their way into the fight or taking a few rounds to – as we say – "have a look". It will be furious from the start. They can both box, but this fight will be decided by the tiniest margins; if either boxer decides to move her feet, pick her punches and show their ring skills, they risk getting lost in the storm.

Once the first bell sounds, they will meet in the centre of the ring. It will stay that way throughout the 10 short rounds. The pattern of the fight is simple to predict, the outcome with any confidence less so. A draw is a great suggestion; a split decision is almost inevitable.

title: Grealish back for Man City - but for how long?
description: Man City winger has made two substitute appearances so far this season, but his future remains in doubt.
fullText:
Jack Grealish is back in the fold at Manchester City... for now.

The 30-year-old is into the final year of his reported £300,000-a-week contract at Etihad Stadium and was discarded by Pep Guardiola in the Spaniard's final season in charge, being allowed to join Everton on a season-long loan deal.

That spell on Merseyside was cut short in January by an Achilles tendon injury, but the Englishman has returned to full fitness and featured in both of City's games so far this season.

Grealish came on during the Community Shield defeat by Arsenal and played the final eight minutes of City's late comeback win over Bournemouth in Sunday's Premier League opener.

The winger appeared to be in good spirits while sitting on the bench against the Cherries and thanked City fans on social media afterwards for a "nice welcome" on his home return.

Though he has been handed a new lease of life under Guardiola's successor Enzo Maresca, no guarantees are being offered that Grealish will remain a City player come transfer deadline day on Tuesday, 1 September.

'Up front next week?' Maresca's Guehi gamble pays off

Grealish was spotted in training when the City players reported for pre-season in mid-July. He was supposed to join his team-mates on the tour of the Far East but was ruled out after suffering an injury setback.

The former Aston Villa skipper has seen Guardiola's departure as a fresh start and impressed in training to such an extent he has earned a place back in the squad.

Heading into the final week of the transfer window, clubs sources have left all options open for Grealish's future - staying at the club, going out on loan again or leaving permanently.

Maresca has not ruled out a move either, saying after Sunday's game: "He is here and it is my duty to coach Jack and to try to get the best.

"Then it is one more week to go and we will see what happens. Not only with Jack but also other players."

Grealish looked to be getting back to his best during his loan at Everton, contributing two goals and six assists in 20 appearances before his injury.

Such was his form at the beginning of last season, he claimed the Premier League's Player of the Month award for August and quickly became a fans' favourite.

City sources say there have been no concrete offers for Grealish so far this summer, with a return to Hill Dickinson Stadium looking the most viable option, should he move away.

Everton are yet to make an approach and try to agree a deal, but he remains of interest to the Toffees.

"He is a player we have remained in contact with," Everton chief executive Angus Kinnear told BBC Radio Merseyside.

"It was no secret he decided to have his injury rehabilitation done here for the remainder of last season - he didn't have to do that as he could have gone back to Manchester City.

"He is a player who has fallen in love with the right shade of blue, but ultimately he is a City player and we have to respect that. What I do know is that the supporters and the team embraced him and treated him as one of our own. That gave us a good platform to have a longer term conversation with him.

"The most important thing is that he is back fit after he had a serious injury, so I was delighted to see him get some minutes in the Community Shield."

title: Jarred Vanderbilt might follow former Lakers teammates steps after Luka Doncic-led preseason trip
description: Los Angeles Lakers forward Jarred Vanderbilt might consider a career-changing move after their recent trip to Slovenia to spend time with Luka Doncic. Doncic invited all his Lakers teammates for the 2026-27 season to his home country of Slovenia, getting to know the players on the massively adjusted roster before a new season.
fullText:
Los Angeles Lakers forward Jarred Vanderbilt might consider a career-changing move after their recent trip to Slovenia to spend time with Luka Doncic.

Doncic invited all his Lakers teammates for the 2026-27 season to his home country of Slovenia, getting to know the players on the massively adjusted roster before a new season.

One of the Lakers players who seemed to have a blast was 27-year-old Vanderbilt, who might be considering a drastic move that a former Lakers teammate made regarding Doncic.

Vanderbilt gave an interview before the Lakers left Slovenia, where he mentioned he is trying to get a Slovenian passport.

"It was amazing… The trip was great. I would love to (come back to Slovenia)… I'm looking to get a Slovenian passport. We'll see. Might be part Slovenian."

Vanderbilt was teammates with Jaxson Hayes for three seasons. Hayes got a Slovenian passport to represent the national team alongside Doncic in future competitions earlier this year.

Vanderbilt might be looking to make a similar move to bolster Doncic's Slovenian squad, especially because he is unlikely to represent Team USA at this point in his career.

The defensive specialist averaged 4.4 points and 4.5 rebounds last season.

If Vanderbilt also joins Slovenia alongside Hayes to bolster their national team, it would be clear evidence that Doncic has recruited role-playing teammates to switch nationalities just to play international basketball for Slovenia.

Given Doncic's play style as an offensive engine, players like Hayes know they can get a featured role alongside Doncic on an otherwise weak Slovenian national team.

Vanderbilt might have severe offensive limitations, but he would easily be the best defender on the Slovenian national team if he were to join.

His size and athleticism would complement FIBA-style basketball, with Doncic's incredible scoring still needed to make up for Vanderbilt's poor scoring.

Joining Luka in Slovenia isn't a guarantee of a future with the Lakers, as Hayes left LA this summer as a free agent, so Vanderbilt's spot as a Laker likely isn't determined by his national team association.
