title: Five Hacks Every Suunto Race 2 User Should Know
description: Automatic laps for my strides? Yes, please.
fullText:
The Suunto Race 2 is an impressive watch, delivering many of the same features of pricier Garmins at a cheaper price. It’s the bigger brother of the Suunto Run, with some capabilities its predecessor doesn't have, such as the ability to access the SuuntoPlus store. There, you can download apps and integrations so your watch can do more than just the default features.

There are some real hidden gems in the SuuntoPlus store, and I’ll share my favorite uses for them below. (Suunto Race 2 users should also check out the Suunto Run hacks since most of them relate to features shared by both watches. )

The Suunto Race 2 can display maps right on the watch, but you need to download those maps before you head out for your adventure. You’ll want to do this at home, on a wifi connection. If you wait until you're at the trailhead to think of it, it will take forever (that is, if you can get the maps to download at all).

To download maps, tap the watch icon at the upper left of the screen, and scroll down to Offline maps. Rather than downloading a specific area, you’ll need to choose one of the available selections. In the U.S., the selections seem to go state-by-state; for example, I can download a Pennsylvania map and a West Virginia map separately, but I can’t download an area that includes bits of both.

Once you have the maps on your watch, you can leave your phone and home and either select Map from your widget list (to see the map without starting an activity), or view the map while navigating during a run.

Even though I knew SuuntoPlus was a big, uh, plus of Suunto’s higher-end sports watches, it took me a long time to realize just what a treasure trove it was. It’s not super clear how to actually use it or what it’s for, so here are the basics.

First, you have to find the SuuntoPlus apps you want. Tap on your watch icon, as you did above, and scroll down to My SuuntoPlus sports apps. If you know the name of the app you want, search for it here; otherwise, browse around.

To use a sports app, you’ll need to select an activity, like a run. Before starting the activity, scroll down and you’ll see a menu called SuuntoPlus. From here, you can select up to three sports apps to run during your activity. Each app will have its own screen in the carousel of data screens. (To move between these screens during the activity, press the dial.)

The SuuntoPlus store also allows you to sync workouts from TrainingPeaks or intervals.icu, or to connect with other devices like the Core 2 temperature sensor. If you’re already a user of one of those services or devices, check out their instructions. I’ll focus here on some of the lesser-known uses of the regular SuuntoPlus sports apps.

If you’ve ever thought your heart rate zones might be incorrect (and they probably are), there’s a SuuntoPlus app that can help. Search for the one called Anaerobic Threshold, and follow the instructions. But be warned: they will lead you through a tough workout. After a warmup, you’ll be asked to run as fast as you can for 30 minutes. At the end, the app will tell you the heart rate that seems to correspond with your lactate threshold.

Now here’s the cool part: on your watch, go into Settings, then Training, then Intensity zones. Choose either the Default HR zones for all sports (what I’d recommend if you aren’t sure) or choose a sport under the advanced setting. Here, you can set the boundaries between your zones. The boundary at the bottom of zone 5 (and thus the top of zone 4) should be set to the number you got from the threshold test. If you’d like to tweak the other zones, Suunto has more information on how to calculate numbers for the other zone boundaries. Unfortunately they are not set automatically.

Cadence is one of the easiest aspects of running form to change on purpose. Cadence means how many steps you take per minute (either per leg, or total). The quicker your steps, the shorter your stride, and the easier it is to keep your landing leg underneath you rather than overstriding. I’ve heard tons of running coaches say that quickening your cadence tends to fix a lot of form problems.

A SuuntoPlus app called Cadence Coach gives you a handy way to work on this, and you may find it useful for your warmups. Install the app, and make sure it’s enabled for your run.

What if that’s not the right cadence for you, at least at this moment? Press the bottom button and the watch will pay attention to your cadence for one minute. Whatever cadence you used in that minute, that is now your target. You can use this feature to give yourself an easier target if you find the recommendation hard to follow, or select a cadence that is appropriate to the workout or terrain that you happen to be doing today.

This is my favorite hack, by far. Stride workouts are a great way to add some speedwork into your routine without needing to measure anything specific, but there’s no easy way to review a stride session after the fact. At least, there isn’t on most watches! The Sprint app on SuuntoPlus gives us a great tool for this exact purpose.

The Sprint app starts by giving you a 10-minute warmup. Whatever pace you run (or walk) during these 10 minutes, the app will assume this is your non-sprinting pace. After this point, just run or walk normally. Anytime you speed up to a sprint (25% or more faster than your warmup pace), the watch will recognize the speed change and mark a new lap for you. It will mark a lap again when you slow down.

There’s a short lag, between five and 10 seconds, each time—so you won’t get surgical precision, but you will get a record of how many strides you did, how long each one was, and approximately how fast you were going during each stride and during the time in between them. The only way I know how to do this on other watches is to either pre-program your strides, or manually press the lap button every time. But this app lets you play them by ear, fartlek-style.

title: Healy right to call out 'vile' abuse - McGivern
description: Linfield chairman Roy McGivern says that manager David Healy was "absolutely right" to call out the "personal" and "vile" abuse directed towards him in recent weeks.
fullText:
Linfield chairman Roy McGivern said that manager David Healy was "absolutely right" to call out the "personal" and "vile" abuse directed towards him in recent weeks.

Healy told the Belfast Telegraph, external that the abuse he, his players and staff received from Blues supporters in Windsor Park and online in the aftermath of their 3-0 defeat by Ballymena United on the opening day of the Irish Premiership season was "nothing short of disgraceful".

McGivern stressed that while Blues supporters had the right to air their frustrations with performances on the pitch, they should not cross the line when it comes to abusing the manager and players.

"I've met with David this week and had a good chat with him. There are certainly no issues between David and the board. We totally understand fans get frustrated, I've been a fan of this club for well over 50 years and fans who pay their money for the games and season tickets and members tickets, they're entitled to give their opinions and be frustrated," McGivern said.

"That's part and parcel of football, we totally get that and no one is saying that's not acceptable.

"What we are saying is, there is a line to be drawn and some of the personal, vile abuse that we've seen both online and in the stands at Windsor Park has just not been acceptable.

"I think David was absolutely right to call that out. I get where fans are coming from but please just show a bit of respect to the players, to the staff, to the directors and other supporters in the stadium."

McGivern also addressed Linfield's financial situation, adding that there are "huge challenges facing the club at the moment".

"It's been a difficult and challenging start to the season. The European tie was one we expected to progress and over the two legs it was a game we should have won but we exit at round one and financially it causes huge issues for the club," he explained.

"I know supporters are concerned. The board would share that concern and we are trying to address the range of financial challenges."

He believes the club need to follow the likes of Coleraine, Glentoran Larne and most recently Cliftonville in accepting outside investment to continue to compete at the top of the table.

"We are in discussion with a number of parties about investment into the club but that all takes time.

"Some of that has appeared in the press recently in terms of the link with Rangers, so we're doing all we can to take that forward whether that is a minority investment or someone taking total ownership of the club.

"All those options are still on the table but the club does need some sort of investment. We can't stand still at this club."

title: Kanter Freedom ejected from WNBA game over player row
description: Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom is ejected from the Women's NBA match between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever after becoming involved in a verbal altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud.
fullText:
Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from Sunday's Women's NBA match between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever after becoming involved in a verbal altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud.

Sitting at courtside, Kanter Freedom stood up with his arms outstretched and took steps towards the court after Cloud began pointing and shouting at him during a timeout.

Kanter Freedom was wearing a T-shirt emblazoned with the words "WOMAN noun. Adult human female.".

Earlier this month, he declared he would enter next season's WNBA Draft, citing the current eligibility guidelines, or lack of, for transgender women players.

Security and other Sky players intervened, before former Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics centre Kanter Freedom was escorted from the court.

He posted on X, external: "I just got kicked out of a WNBA game for supporting WOMEN! Let that sink in, AMERICA!"

Writing on Threads, external after the game, Cloud said: "To every trans kid/person, you are apart of MY community & tribe. You belong. You're loved. You're seen. You're perfect as you are & you will always be protected by me."

Kanter Freedom reportedly spoke with police officers before exiting Chicago's Wintrust Arena.

The Fever won the match 113-90.

"There's so many good things about this league and so many good things about the play of these players, that if you come to a game, you should probably come to enjoy the basketball," said Sky head coach Tyler Marsh.

"That seems pretty simple to me. I think these players deserve that and have earned that. Being a former basketball player, you should probably understand and feel that, too."

The transgender controversy surrounding the WNBA

Sex toys again thrown on court during WNBA matches

On Saturday, the Sky's win over Golden State Valkyries was one of two WNBA matches interrupted after sex toys were thrown on to the court.

There were similar incidents last season when six WNBA matches in Atlanta, New York and Los Angeles were interrupted.

USA Today, external reported the same group responsible for last year's incidents has said it will continue to disrupt WNBA games to protest against the league's policy on transgender athletes.

The WNBA operates under a collective bargaining agreement (CBA), a deal negotiated between the league and its players association (WNBPA), setting rules on matters including player salary caps, revenue sharing, benefits and overall league operations.

On player eligibility, the CBA states: "Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA."

There are no transgender athletes currently competing in the league, but intense debate in the US has been sparked by recent comments from Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham - who played in Sunday's match in Chicago - questioning the current rules.

title: Rogers & Palmer star but Sanchez struggles - Fulham v Chelsea player ratings
description: Morgan Rogers scores on his Chelsea debut as Xabi Alonso's side beat Fulham at Craven Cottage - here are BBC Sport's player ratings.
fullText:
Morgan Rogers scored on his Chelsea debut as Xabi Alonso's side beat Fulham at Craven Cottage.

The £117m signing slotted in his side's second goal after Fulham midfielder Josh King had cancelled out Joao Pedro's opener, which came within 31 seconds.

Cole Palmer thought he had sealed victory for Chelsea with a third goal early in the second half before debutant striker Gonzalo Garcia gave Fulham hope but the visitors held on to start the season with a win.

Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them at the bottom of the page too.

Three reasons Chelsea could challenge for title - and one they may not

Palmer shines as Alonso begins Chelsea reign with win at Fulham

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Bernd Leno: The German goalkeeper was not particularly at fault for any of Chelsea's goals but still couldn't stop them. 5

Timothy Castagne: The right-back set up King's goal and his shot led to Fulham's second, but he struggled defensively. 6

Jorge Cuenca: His poor clearance and mistimed tackle led to Chelsea's opening goal. He was also at fault for the second, failing to stop Lacroix's cross. However, his lofted pass helped create Fulham's second goal. 4

Calvin Bassey: Less culpable than many of his defensive team-mates, but still part of a disappointing display at the back. 5

Antonee Robinson: The United States international produced an important early block from a Rogers effort and delivered an excellent cross later in the first half, but was often caught out of position on the counter-attack. He lofted a finish well wide in the 77th minute with his weaker right foot when one-on-one with Sanchez. 6

Sander Berge: Struggled to dictate the tempo as he had done in pre-season in an unsettled game. 5

Josh King: The academy graduate was Fulham's standout performer, creating chances and posing a threat before scoring the first-half equaliser. Almost produced an equaliser in the 73rd minute from range. 8

Alex Iwobi: The Nigeria international provided a strong physical presence both defensively and in attack. 6

Oscar Bobb: The Norway international's direct running caused problems down the right, although his influence faded as the game wore on. 7

Gonzalo Garcia: On his debut, Garcia provided a useful focal point in attack in a difficult match for Fulham. He helped relieve pressure after long spells of Chelsea possession and was rewarded with a close-range header in the second half. 7

Cesar Palacios: The new signing worked hard on his debut, but little came off for him, including a long-range effort that flew well over the bar in the first half. 5

Shea Charles (on 67, Bobb): The new signing from Southampton produced some dangerous long balls as Fulham pushed for an equaliser. 6

Kevin (on 73, Palacios): Did little to influence the game. 5

Ryan Sessegnon (on 73, Berge): His running in-behind threatened down the left and he forced a good save from Sanchez. 6

Rodrigo Muniz (on 82, Robinson): 5

Subs not used: Lecomte, De Gougerolles, Tete, Reed, Kevin, Smith Rowe.

Robert Sanchez: An early kicking error gifted Fulham a corner. He should have saved King's equaliser at his near post, while his initial save for Fulham's second was parried into a dangerous area, allowing Garcia to score. 3

Josh Acheampong: The 20-year-old produced a fine double clearance and block in the 27th minute and looked solid throughout. 6

Maxence Lacroix: Remarkably involved in both of Chelsea's first two goals, with his headed clearance leading to the opener and his run down the right and cut-back setting up Rogers. 7

Levi Colwill: An early mistake left him fortunate to escape with only a yellow card after a foul on Bobb. He was also partly at fault for Fulham's second goal after failing to clear a deep cross. 5

Malo Gusto: The wing-back was a surprise selection amid Chelsea's injury problems, but his passing lacked conviction at times. 5

Romeo Lavia: Booked early on after a late challenge on Bassey. He grew into the game, however, going close from a corner and moving the ball well through midfield. 5

Reece James: Saw a miscued effort saved in the first half but gradually grew into the game and helped Chelsea gain control. 6

Jorrel Hato: Operating in an unfamiliar wing-back role, the defender produced a promising early dribble and adapted well. 6

Cole Palmer: Simply the best player on the pitch. Palmer was creative, physically impressive and produced several superb dribbles before scoring an excellent third goal. He looks refreshed after the summer break. 9

Morgan Rogers: An outstanding debut. Pressed aggressively, had a shot blocked, played in Joao Pedro and then capped his display by scoring Chelsea's second with a far-post finish. 8

Joao Pedro: Opened the scoring after 31 seconds with a deft finish over Leno. He also exploited Fulham's high defensive line intelligently to set up Palmer's goal. 8

Enzo Fernandez (on 65, Lavia): The Argentine was booed by the home fans on every touch of the ball and might not have featured had Moises Caicedo been fit. Still, Fernandez moved the ball around the pitch and fought for possession. 6

Pep Chavarria (on 65, Hato): It was a back-to-the-wall job for the wing-back but he did little of note on his brief debut cameo. 5

Geovany Quenda (on 82, Rogers): 5

Subs not used: Penders, Barco, Gittens, Welbeck.

title: England World Cup hopes end after Netherlands draw
description: England's chances of World Cup glory are over after they draw 2-2 with the Netherlands.
fullText:
England's World Cup hopes are over after they drew 2-2 with the Netherlands in their final Pool E game.

Zak Jones' side had to beat the co-hosts to have a chance of progressing from the second pool stage to the semi-finals.

They went ahead after five minutes through Stuart Rushmere, but the Netherlands, three-time World Cup winners, responded through Jip Janssen and Thierry Brinkman.

Henry Croft levelled for England early in the fourth quarter, but they could not find a winner in Amstelveen.

"[I am] gutted, heartbroken. It hurts a lot," said England captain Zach Wallace.

"We gave it everything and we put in a performance we can be proud of. In the end it wasn't to be.

"Some decisions fell against us and some balls didn't fall our way. It's those details at the top level."

The result means the Netherlands top the group and advance to the semi-finals from Pool E along with Argentina, with England third and India in fourth.

Germany and Spain complete the semi-final line-up.

England's final game of the tournament will be the fifth-place match against Australia at the same stadium on Friday (14:00 BST).

title: Villa in talks with Club Brugge for defender Ordonez
description: Aston Villa are working on a move for Club Brugge central defender Joel Ordonez after failing to agree a deal with Southampton for Taylor Harwood-Bellis.
fullText:
Aston Villa are working to sign Club Brugge central defender Joel Ordonez after failing to agree a deal with Southampton for Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

The Premier League side, who sold England defender Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last week, are accelerating their interest in Ordonez, with discussions ongoing and his Belgian Pro League club wanting a minimum £40m fee for the Ecuador international.

The 22-year-old centre-back, who played for his country at this summer's World Cup, has made 124 appearances for Club Brugge since joining in 2022 from Independiente del Valle.

Villa had targeted Harwood-Bellis, but there is understood to be a significant gap in valuation between them and Southampton after an offer worth £18m was rejected.

It remains to be seen whether a transfer for the 24-year-old can still be revived but, as things stand, Unai Emery's side have moved on to other targets.

Villa lost their opening game of the season 4-0 to Brighton on Sunday and are working to strengthen their squad before the transfer deadline on 1 September.

They have lost a host of key players this season with Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Konsa all departing.

There are also questions over Ollie Watkins' future with the striker a target for Al-Hilal in Saudi Arabia.

title: Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?
description: After every round of Premier League matches this season, Troy Deeney gives us his team of the week. Do you agree with his choices?
fullText:
After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.

Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.

James Trafford (Leeds): It's been a big-pressure move for Trafford going to Leeds. I think at the World Cup with England he thought, 'I should be playing more' and he obviously didn't get the time and needed a move away. He produced a strong performance for Leeds at Nottingham Forest and was one of the few goalkeepers to keep a clean sheet.

Keane Lewis-Potter (Brentford): He was excellent defensively and attacking wise and got his goal. He is one of Brentford's underrated players and sort of sums up their team. Nobody speaks about him or Brentford but they hammered Tottenham.

Nobel Mendy (Hull City): He was so good and powerful. He offered so much defensively to Hull and scored their second goal. He was a real powerhouse. Hull will definitely need him and he is one of those defenders where you think, 'I don't want to play against him'.

Maxence Lacroix (Chelsea): Lacroix just added a level of experience and calmness to Chelsea and also got an assist. He read the game and understood what was needed and provided the maturity that will add so much to Chelsea going forward. It was a very good debut for the France defender.

Maxim de Cuyper (Brighton): He scored two goals and was excellent for Brighton. Opponents Aston Villa were poor, but if you watched the first 20 minutes you would see he was really aggressive and really set the tone with the pressure.

Marc Guehi (Man City): I'll have Guehi in as my holding midfielder. He should have scored two against Bournemouth because he missed a massive chance before he ended up scoring. But he got the equaliser and offered a lot more of a calming presence than City's £116m record signing Elliot Anderson - Guehi controlled the game a little bit more.

Vitaly Janelt (Brentford): He is one of those big, powerful and dominant players who does the basics really well. He mixed that with a goal against Spurs and you don't really speak about him, but he was always the one breaking up play and doing the horrible things really well.

Christos Tzolis (Arsenal): A lot of people are talking about Arsenal and how they're great. That is absolutely true. And so is the bit of business they did bringing this young man in from Club Brugge. So many goals and assists he brings to the team, but also a calming influence and tenacity as well. Look at Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, he feels to me like both of them in one. He has a lot more output than those guys. He's going to be a beast for this year.

Anthony Elanga (Newcastle): Last season I though he was treated poorly by Eddie Howe because he was one that kept being put on the bench, being introduced late or would be the first one to come off. But he showed in a new formation, under a new manager and somebody who believes in him that he can use his pace and power. As a result he looks like a completely different player and he looked happy. He ran past Milos Kerkez like he wasn't there despite the Liverpool left-back having a five-yard start and produced an unbelievable finish for his goal.

Cole Palmer (Chelsea): One we were all talking about, and should've gone to the World Cup with England. Feels like he's got a point to prove, feels like he's been working hard. The injuries from last year skewed everyone's vision. This is going to be a breakout season for him. Everything he did was positive. Ran forward with pace, looked like he could move. He had those issues with the groin but now he's chopping and turning.

Joao Pedro (Chelsea): My old Watford team-mate and someone who will make everyone question when they said he wasn't good enough. He's going to have a breakout year.

Sergej Jakirovic (Hull City): Tactically brilliant and had a gameplan for Manchester United. His side gave a bit of space away but wouldn't get transitioned on, gave away a lot of cheap fouls. Went forward in the wide areas, crossed it and finished the action. He was very impressive in the Championship last year, spoke well but never got too high or too low. He'll take a few by surprise but I'm concerned they won't have the quality in the team. For now, who cares?

title: Forest working on deal for Chelsea striker Delap
description: Nottingham Forest are working on a deal to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap.
fullText:
Nottingham Forest are working on a deal to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap.

The 23-year-old has been made available for sale by Chelsea for £50m and is training separately from the first-team squad.

It remains unclear whether the talks are over a permanent transfer or a loan move, but the two clubs are known to have a positive working relationship.

Delap was left out of Chelsea's squad for Monday's Premier League match against Fulham and lost the number nine shirt to fellow forward Joao Pedro last week.

His potential departure comes just over 12 months after moving to Stamford Bridge for £30m from Ipswich Town, but he ended the season with just one league goal after shoulder and hamstring injuries.

Forest have signed defender Ousmane Diomande from Sporting for £34m, alongside free agents, midfielder Xaver Schlager and keeper Steve Benda, so far this summer.

However, they have sold England midfielder Elliot Anderson to Manchester City for a club-record £116m and striker Taiwo Awoniyi to Coventry City for £9m.

Delap's arrival would provide competition for Chris Wood and Igor Jesus at the City Ground.

Chelsea, meanwhile, are looking to sanction a number of sales and loan departures before the transfer deadline on 1 September, and currently have 39 senior players on their books.

title: 2 children among 4 killed in Gaza a week after US asked Israel to curb attacks
description: DEIR AL-BALAH, Gaza Strip (AP) — Palestinian residents of war-battered Gaza fled homes and businesses as Israeli strikes and tank fire killed at least four people Monday, including two children, hospi...
fullText:
DEIR AL-BALAH, Gaza Strip (AP) — Palestinian residents of war-battered Gaza fled homes and businesses as Israeli strikes and tank fire killed at least four people Monday, including two children, hospital officials said, a week after a U.S. delegation asked Israel to draw down attacks.

After evacuation warnings by Israel's military, a strike hit a building in the Bureij refugee camp in central Gaza. One family was unable to flee and a 4-year-old child was killed, according to Awda Hospital, where he was taken. His mother and sister were wounded. There was no Israeli military comment.

Israeli strikes hit three other buildings across the territory after residents said they received evacuation warnings. Some people sprinted away, with mothers carrying children, while others moved amid the rubble in wheelchairs or with canes.

Smoke rose over the already devastated landscape.

Israel's military said it carried out strikes in the Shati refugee camp in Gaza City and in Deir al-Balah after issuing warnings, targeting what it described as two Hamas weapons storage facilities inside mosques. The military did not provide evidence but said the facilities contained dozens of "Kalashnikov rifles, magazines and additional military equipment."

An earlier Israeli strike on a tent in Deir al-Balah killed a man, according to Al-Aqsa Hospital, where his body was taken. Israel's military said it killed a militant affiliated with Hamas' special forces unit.

A man was killed and five others were wounded in an Israeli strike in Khan Younis in southern Gaza, according to Nasser Hospital, which received the casualties.

And Israeli tank fire hit an area east of Khan Younis, killing a 10-year-old girl, according to the hospital, where her body was taken.

Israel's military did not immediately comment on the strike in Khan Younis and said it was not aware of the incident with the child.

Israel has continued to carry out targeted killings in the week since a U.S. delegation met with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in an effort to push last year's ceasefire deal forward.

U.S. negotiator Jared Kushner asked Netanyahu to draw down Israel's attacks in Gaza, a person familiar with the meeting said last week, speaking on condition of anonymity because they weren't authorized to brief journalists.

Israel has announced strikes on six of the seven days since that meeting.

While the heaviest fighting in Gaza has subsided since the ceasefire took hold in October, Israeli airstrikes have killed at least 1,288 Palestinians, according to Gaza's health ministry. The ministry, part of the Hamas-led government, maintains detailed casualty records that are seen as generally reliable by U.N. agencies and independent experts. It does not give a breakdown of civilians and militants.

Militants have carried out shooting attacks on Israeli troops, and Israel says its strikes are in response to that and other ceasefire violations. Five Israeli soldiers have been killed since the ceasefire.

Palestinian officials have reported strikes on homes and police stations, and Hamas has claimed that attacks are designed to destabilize Gaza and prevent progress on the ceasefire's next steps, which include demilitarizing and reconstructing the territory and the deployment of an international stabilization force.

In the period before the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attack on southern Israel that sparked the war, burning kites and balloons were sent from Gaza into Israel, causing fires and other damage.

Now Israeli officials are expressing concern after several kites were found in a kibbutz near Gaza. No weapons or dangerous materials were attached. Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz in a statement Sunday threatened to ramp up strikes on Gaza unless Hamas ensures the kites stop flying toward Israel.

Hamas spokesperson Hazem Qassem has called the kites "essentially children's toys" and accused Israel of using them as "an attempt to justify the continuation of aggression and violations against our people."

The Oct. 7 attack killed some 1,200 people and saw 251 taken hostage. All hostages or their remains were later released. Israel's retaliatory offensive in Gaza has killed more than 73,422 Palestinians, according to Gaza's health ministry.

AlJoud reported from Beirut. AP writer Sam Metz in Jerusalem contributed to this report.

California, along with Texas, already requires content creators to include payment disclaimers on their political posts. The legislation, which was authored by Democratic Assemblymember Marc Berman, will need a final vote in the Assembly before it can reach Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom's desk.

Chatbots can produce complex arguments, often quoting regulations or acts of Parliament, with documents running to dozens of pages long. title: Hodgkinson withdraws from Zurich Diamond League
description: Keely Hodgkinson withdraws from the women's 800 metres at Thursday's Diamond League meeting in Zurich because her "body is not quite ready".
fullText:
Keely Hodgkinson has withdrawn from the women's 800 metres at Thursday's Diamond League meeting in Zurich because her "body is not quite ready".

Olympic champion Hodgkinson had been set to go head-to-head with Switzerland's Audrey Werro, who beat the Briton to gold at the European Championships in Birmingham earlier this month.

"Unfortunately the body isn't quite ready to race again after the European Championships," Hodgkinson said in a statement.

"We've made the decision to skip this race and get ready for the next one. Sad to miss it, hopefully see you next year!"

The race will feature world 400m hurdles champion Femke Broeders-Bol, who has stepped up to the 800m this season, and Hodgkinson's training partner Georgia Hunter-Bell, who won 800m gold at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow last month.

World 800m champion Lilian Odira of Kenya, who beat Hodgkinson and Hunter-Bell to gold in Tokyo last year, has pulled out of the race after suffering from illness and weakness since the Commonwealth Games.

While Diamond League organisers said they were looking forward to Hodgkinson's "highly anticipated race against Audrey Werro", they "fully respect" the Briton's decision and "hope to see her back in Zurich in the future".

After suffering hamstring and knee injuries over the past few years, Hodgkinson skipped the Commonwealth Games to prioritise the European Championships amid a busy summer schedule.

"I signed myself up for Zurich because I knew everyone was in it but me. I want to be in with the best and I think that's going to bring out the best in me," Hodgkinson said in Birmingham earlier this month.

Before winning 800m gold at the London Diamond League on 18 July, Hodgkinson said she was feeling "definitely a lot better than I was".

Thursday's meet in Zurich is the penultimate Diamond League event of the season, with the final to take place in Brussels over two days on Friday 4 and Saturday 5 September.

title: Three reasons Chelsea could challenge for title - and one they may not
description: While Chelsea's front three produced a sparkling display in their win over Fulham, goalkeeper Robert Sanchez remains a major concern.
fullText:
If football is won in both boxes, it seems as though Chelsea have one far better covered than the other.

Xabi Alonso began his Stamford Bridge reign with an entertaining 3-2 Premier League win at west London rivals Fulham on Monday - and their new-look front three stole the show.

Morgan Rogers, making his debut after his club record £117m summer move from Aston Villa, combined with Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro to produce a devastating attacking display.

All three scored, with Palmer in particular looking back to his best after a difficult year hampered by injuries, culminating in his omission from England's World Cup squad.

At the other end, though, questions remain over goalkeeper Robert Sanchez after two errors contributed to Fulham's goals from Josh King and Gonzalo Garcia.

Alonso said his front three needed to "lead the rest" so that the "other ones will follow".

But Sanchez has some catching up to do - and when asked about his mistakes, Alonso could only stress the collective responsibility of the team.

"We need to accept and learn from them [the mistakes]," said the Spaniard. "This is going to be a process.

"All the lines, from the strikers, the midfielders, the defence, the goalkeepers, we want to do better in everything."

After the match, ex-Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher - a former team-mate of Alonso - said on Sky Sports that Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro are "as good as anything in the Premier League right now".

He also said they would they "will never win the league with Sanchez in goal".

Palmer shines as Alonso begins Chelsea reign with win at Fulham

Rogers & Palmer star but Sanchez struggles - Fulham v Chelsea player ratings

It took Joao Pedro just 31 seconds to open the scoring, latching on to a pass from Palmer and lifting his shot over Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno for Chelsea's fastest goal since October 2016.

After King had equalised, Rogers then marked his debut with a goal before half-time by tapping in from close range.

But it was Palmer - scorer of Chelsea's third - who stood out most.

He has endured a frustrating 18 months since a niggling groin problem disrupted his sensational start to life at Stamford Bridge, highlighted by the fact he matched last season's Premier League assist tally by setting up Joao Pedro.

His trickery and creativity was on display throughout against Fulham, along with an impressive work-rate. This was more like the Palmer we saw during his first season at Stamford Bridge - and like the one who tore Paris St-Germain apart during last year's Club World Cup final.

"Over the summer I rested, I recharged and, yeah, I'm ready and I'm hungry," Palmer, who is now just two goals away from 50 in the Premier League, told Sky Sports.

During Chelsea's pre-season tour of Australia, he spoke of having a point to prove and admitted a lengthy summer break felt unusual after featuring in major tournaments in each of the previous three years.

"Cole Palmer was sensational," said former Manchester United defender Gary Neville on Sky Sports. "Him and Morgan Rogers were electric with Joao Pedro - the front three were brilliant.

"That tonight was the old Cole Palmer. It was unbelievable to watch. One of the best things I've seen this weekend."

While Palmer and Joao Pedro have generally carried Chelsea's biggest attacking threat in recent times, they have now been joined by the impressive Rogers too.

His arrival reunites him with Palmer, an ex-Manchester City team-mate and someone he described after the win at Craven Cottage as his "best friend in football".

"He had a difficult season with injuries and stuff last year - and you could see it in his eyes in pre-season and training that he's ready this year and ready to prove people wrong," added Rogers when asked about Palmer's display.

"You saw that with that performance. He was the best player on the pitch by a mile and that's what he does. It's good to have him on our side."

Indeed, it was also encouraging how Rogers, whose pre-season was shortened by his involvement in England's run to third place at the World Cup, looked so fit and powerful.

Rogers is the first Chelsea player to score on his Premier League debut since Christopher Nkunku in 2023 - and the first to create five chances in his first league appearance since records began in 2003-04.

It was also the first time Chelsea supporters sang the new Rogers chant in the away end.

Like Palmer, Joao Pedro missed out on the World Cup - as a high-profile omission from Brazil's squad - but returned in pre-season with eight goals in seven games.

It was no surprise to see him on the scoresheet so early in the Premier League campaign, having inherited the number nine shirt from Liam Delap, who was left out of the squad on Monday, following the contract extension the Brazilian signed this weekend.

"Great combination, great quality," Alonso told BBC Match of the Day when asked about his front three.

"We know if we reach them [Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer] in good positions, they have this talent to create special things and I am very happy the three forwards have scored.

"We need to put them in the best situations. I am happy for the three of them. They played for the team."

Yet questions remain over Sanchez, who allowed King's low strike to go straight through him for Fulham's equaliser and then tamely parried Timothy Castagne's shot into a dangerous area for Garcia to head in from close range to set up a nervy finish.

"They have strengthened in every position of the pitch but you cannot take a chance on goalkeepers," said Neville.

"I've said before it's the most difficult position on the pitch, it's the one that carries the most scrutiny and if you have got a goalkeeper who's making mistakes and is anxious, it will undermine everything you're trying to do.

"It's a problem. You've got to say it's a problem."

There was nowhere to hide for Sanchez.

King's equaliser in the 23rd minute had an expected goals on target (xGoT) value of just 0.05, making it the lowest-rated shot to result in a goal during the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

In other words, Sanchez really should have saved it.

He did make a number of other saves, but he also conceded a corner after failing to clear the ball before it ran out of play and was later unconvincing when coming off his line to deal with a long ball, with Antonee Robinson missing the target to let him off the hook.

While Alonso defended his goalkeeper after the game, in his pre-match news conference on Thursday, he said: "The pitch is the boss of everything. I don't decide. The players need to show me."

That message applied to his goalkeepers - Sanchez and number two Mike Penders, 21, who is waiting to make his debut after returning from a successful loan spell at Strasbourg.

With the transfer window still open, many Chelsea fans will be asking whether the club need a new first-choice goalkeeper.

As Carragher said: "They have to sort the goalkeeping issue out because it's going to come back and haunt them again this season as it did tonight."

title: Punishment that sends shiver down whole England team needed - Vaughan
description: A punishment to “send a shiver down the whole team” may be needed after Brydon Carse became the latest England cricketer involved in a drinking controversy, according to Michael Vaughan.
fullText:
A punishment to "send a shiver down the whole team" may be needed after Brydon Carse became the latest England cricketer involved in a drinking controversy, according to Michael Vaughan.

Pace bowler Carse was briefly placed under arrest on a night out with his Durham team-mates in Derby at the weekend.

The incident is being investigated by the Cricket Regulator and, as a result, Carse has been removed from the England squad for the second Test against Pakistan at Lord's on Thursday.

"Someone is going to have to get a punishment that sends a shiver down the whole England cricket team and right down through the programme, so that everyone knows that if you misbehave or bring any kind of bad reputation on to this team, you know what's going to come," former England captain Vaughan told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"It's the only punishment that will really hurt players."

In October, England white-ball captain Harry Brook was punched by a bouncer outside a nightclub in Wellington, New Zealand, with team-mates Jacob Bethell and Josh Tongue also present.

During the Ashes tour of Australia, opener Ben Duckett was filmed apparently drunk on England's holiday in Noosa.

And in June, former Test captain Ben Stokes and pace bowler Gus Atkinson broke a team curfew and were present when a member of England's security staff was punched by a Saracens rugby player in a London nightclub.

In this latest incident, Carse was with Durham team-mates Stokes and Matthew Potts, all of whom are under England central contracts. In Stokes' case, the England deal remains in place despite his international retirement in June.

It makes a total of eight contracted players who have been involved in or present for late-night incidents in the past year – more than a quarter of the 30 men on England deals.

In this latest occurrence, footage shared on social media on Sunday showed Carse in handcuffs, surrounded by police officers.

Listen to Vaughan, Tufnell and Finn discuss Carse incident on the TMS podcast

And, although Vaughan said it is an "awful look for the England team once again", he would "feel" for Carse if he is made an example of following the other events of the past year.

"I hope Carse is getting good support around him," said Vaughan. "He is a character who can be a little bit loose and if you give him a bit of rope he'll take a huge amount of it. He needs people around him who are giving him better advice.

"I would feel for Carse if he is the one who takes the rap for what has happened over the past nine months, but somewhere, somehow, something has to be done to set a precedent that they won't stand for that behaviour any more."

On Monday, the England and Wales Cricket Board confirmed that the Regulator was investigating and, as a result, 31-year-old Carse had been removed from the squad for the second Test, with his place going to Sonny Baker.

Soon after that, Derbyshire Police said a man in his 30s was arrested on Saturday night, only to be de-arrested a short time later.

"A man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly in Derby city centre on Saturday night, 22 August," said a police statement.

"However the man was de-arrested shortly afterwards having agreed to leave the area."

This new controversy comes only one game into Joe Root's second spell as Test captain.

Before his first game back in charge, an innings defeat of Pakistan at Headingley, Root called on his players to be "good role models and good human beings".

Now, Root will speak to the media on Tuesday to address the fallout from the Carse incident.

"Joe Root will be absolutely fuming with this," said Vaughan. "He will have been hoping to arrive at Lord's to talk about cricket and his team.

"Now he will have to answer all these questions about discipline, curfews and drinking culture.

"Everything we thought has been brushed under the carpet and moved to one side, we are pretty much back to square one."

Former England spinner Phil Tufnell agreed with Vaughan that a substantial punishment is the only way to ensure players fall in line.

Tufnell, who had multiple brushes with authority during his international career, said: "If you want to stop this, the only way you stop it is say: 'You're not playing for five games.'

"I was made to stand in the corner during my England career, was told: 'You're not available for selection.' It will soon stop. It would be cleared up in a jiffy."

Carse was in the England squad for the first Test but not selected in the final XI. It is unlikely he would have been in the team for the second Test at Lord's, unless one of England's four frontline seamers from Headingley suffered a fitness issue.

Since Carse made his Test debut in October 2024, no England bowler has more Test wickets than his 58. He was the only member of England's attack to play all five matches in the Ashes series in Australia.

However, he was unavailable at the beginning of the home summer because of an injury, and being removed from the squad for the second Test could push him further down the pecking order.

"Carse is 31 and coming to the autumn of his career," said Tufnell. "You need to keep yourself fit.

"You want to be bowling these long spells for England and making a name for yourself.

"It's probably best not to be doing that [going out so late]. Some of the best in the business have tried and failed at doing that."

title: Watson among Britons through in US Open qualifying
description: Heather Watson is among the British winners in the first round of US Open qualifying as she bids for a first New York main-drawn appearance in five years.
fullText:
Britain's Heather Watson battled back from a set down against Claire Liu to keep alive her hopes of securing a first US Open main-draw appearance in five years.

The 34-year-old Watson beat sixth seed Liu 4-6 6-2 6-4 in the first round of qualifying in New York.

Watson almost let a double-break lead slip in the final set but held firm to set up a meeting with Spain's Angela Fita Boluda.

Toby Samuel, Jacob Fearnley, Billy Harris and Harry Wendelken all progressed in men's qualifying.

Samuel, seeking to reach the US Open main draw for the first time, fought back against Italy's Francesco Maestrelli to win 6-7 (2-7) 6-3 6-1 and set up a meeting with fellow Briton Harris.

Harris progressed with a 6-1 6-3 win against Peru's Gonzalo Bueno.

Fearnley claimed a 7-6 (7-3) 6-3 victory over Spain's Roberto Carballes Baena to set up a meeting with Frenchman Luka Pavlovic.

Wendelken will meet Swiss player Remy Bertola after overcoming Italy's Stefano Travaglia 6-4 3-6 6-3.

However, Liam Broady lost 7-6 (7-4) 6-3 against Italy's Marco Cecchinato, while Felix Gill was beaten by Italian Francesco Passaro 7-6 (7-3) 6-2.

Players must come through three rounds of qualifying to reach the singles main draw, which gets under way on Sunday.

Williams and Alcaraz to play US Open mixed doubles

Injured Sinner & Draper withdraw from US Open

China's two-time US Open quarter-finalist Zheng Qinwen, contesting a Grand Slam qualifying event for the first time since the 2022 Australian Open, defeated compatriot Xiaodi You 6-3 6-2.

The 23-year-old, who has fallen to 121st in the world since undergoing elbow surgery last year, will meet France's Clara Burel next.

Meanwhile, Brazilian world number 26 Joao Fonseca has announced he will miss the tournament because of an abdominal injury.

The 20-year-old French Open quarter-finalist said he would require "more time to fully recover so I can compete at a high level".

In the mixed doubles competition, Britons Henry Patten and Lloyd Glasspool will both seek to beat some of the sport's biggest stars after coming through two qualifying matches on Monday.

The US Open mixed doubles was controversially revamped last year to include singles stars in a bid to attract more attention to the format.

Under the new format, the top six pairs with the best combined singles rankings received direct entry into the main draw, with another eight receiving wildcards.

The tournament now takes place over three days in the week before the main draw began, and features a shorter scoring system with only four games required to win a set in matches before the final, no 'advantage' scoring and 10-point match tie-breaks instead of a third set throughout.

Both Patten and Glasspool had to come through qualifying with their respective partners on Monday.

Patten, a two-time winner of the men's doubles competition at Wimbledon, and Czech team-mate Katerina Siniakova defeated Americans Peyton Stearns and Christian Harrison in straight sets in their second qualifying match.

Next, Patten and Siniakova - the respective men's and women's world number ones in doubles - will take on 24-time major winner Novak Djokovic and top-ranked Aryna Sabalenka in the first round of the main draw.

After defeating El Salvador's Marcelo Arevalo and France's Kristina Mladenovic, Glasspool and New Zealand's Erin Routliffe will face 23-time Grand Slam singles champion Serena Williams and seven-time major winner Carlos Alcaraz.

Alcaraz will be playing his first match in four months after recovering from a wrist injury, while Williams is making her return to the sport after a four-year absence.

title: Why one of Trump’s favorite economic statistics is nearly meaningless
description: President Donald Trump says not to believe the many polls finding that most Americans disapprove of his handling of the economy. On Friday, to argue that his numbers should be much better, he cited a nearly meaningless fact he portrayed as a major accomplishment.
fullText:
President Donald Trump says not to believe the many polls finding that most Americans disapprove of his handling of the economy. On Friday, to argue that his numbers should be much better, he cited a nearly meaningless fact he portrayed as a major accomplishment.

"I'll see a poll," he said at a rally in South Carolina, "and it'll say, 'Trump is at 44% on the economy.' How can it be at 44? We have more people working now than ever before."

Trump heralded the same fact later in the speech: "Remember when I say, and I'll say it again and again: There are more people working today in the United States of America than at any time in the history of our country." And then, emphasizing the supposed importance of the fact, he repeated it a third time.

It's not clear whether Trump is genuinely unaware this fact is insignificant or whether he is knowingly hyping an insignificant fact for political gain. Regardless, touting the fact "again and again" is unlikely to do anything for his economic approval — because the fact tells us almost nothing about the state of the economy.

The number of people working in the US generally rises over time simply because the population rises over time. With the exception of recessions, like those caused by the financial crisis of 2008 or the Covid-19 crisis of 2020, the number of employed people tends to just get higher as the years pass.

"There are more Americans working because there are more Americans. That's the entire analysis," Justin Wolfers, a University of Michigan professor of public policy and economics, wrote in his newsletter earlier this month.

Every US president since at least 1948, when modern federal data collection began, could have accurately said at some point during their tenure that more people were working in the US than ever before. That clearly isn't because each of these presidents was presiding over a pristine economy.

The cost of living, not the state of the labor market, has almost certainly been the key driver of Trump's dismal economic polling this year. But even if you're looking only at jobs, there are much better ways to gauge the situation than the statistic Trump keeps citing. These other metrics show his second-term economy is far from historically strong.

You can look, for example, at the employment-population ratio, which measures the percentage of the population ages 16 and over that is employed. It's down from 60.1% in January 2025, the month of Trump's second inauguration, to 58.9% in July 2026 — lower than it was during the entirety of Joe Biden's last three years as president.

title: Victims describe 'house of terror' abuse by mother, grandmother and stepfather
description: Shirley Freeman, Julia Stephen and David McColl's victims were beaten, starved and psychologically tormented.
fullText:
A mother, grandmother and stepfather who subjected three children to years of abuse in a "house of terror" have avoided jail.

Shirley Freeman, Julia Stephen and David McColl's victims were beaten, starved and psychologically tormented between 2003 and 2012.

Freeman, 51, and Stephen, 69, were earlier found guilty of cruel and unnatural treatment. McColl, 50, admitted the crimes.

At Aberdeen Sheriff Court, Sheriff Craig Findlater said no sentence could "repair the awful childhoods" of the trio's victims.

Warning: This article contains descriptions of child abuse

Freeman was sentenced to 18 months probation, 240 hours of unpaid work, and a 12-month restriction of liberty order, as a direct alternative to custody.

Stephen was ordered to carry out 150 hours of unpaid work and given 18 months probation.

And McColl was sentenced to 220 hours of unpaid work, 18 months probation, and an 11-month restriction of liberty order.

Victims William and Meaghann Murphy, who are now 25 and 28, told BBC Scotland News the violence and cruelty they experienced as children became normal.

William said he was "utterly disappointed" at what he described as the "leniency" of the sentence.

"Violence and psychological terror resulted in nothing more than unpaid work and a curfew," he said.

"This system has failed my sisters and me, but we refuse to let it silence us. We must do better. We must stop child abusers from walking away with a slap on the wrist."

Their younger sister, Rebekah Simpson, 23, said the abuse she received had had a lifelong impact on her mental and physical health.

She said she felt that the court did not fully consider the impact the experience had had on her - but she was not disappointed with the sentences.

"Not having to speak to them again is justice for me," she said.

"I want to be able to walk the streets and know they will be punished if they try and approach me."

The abuse happened at an address in Balloch, Dunbartonshire, and at a flat in Aberdeen's Bedford Avenue.

A trial heard that Freeman, now of Cullen, Moray, had created a "house of terror" for the children.

"The things that stick out for me were the anger, the violent outbursts that would come from my mother," Meaghann said.

"William and I were both locked in a room and because I was bursting for the toilet I had to take all my clothes out of my bottom drawer and use that.

"She went ballistic about it. I got slapped about for that. After that, instead of letting us out the room, she just put a bucket in the room.

"So my experience from the get-go has been just straight-up cruelty."

She described being deprived of food for days at a time and said locks were placed on cupboards to prevent the children helping themselves.

The court heard Freeman repeatedly struck the children with a metal-studded belt.

William said: "For as long as I can remember, family life was chaotic and unpredictable, and at times quite hostile. We were often made to sleep on the floor as a punishment.

"Sometimes when we had been really bad, they called it sleep deprivation, where they got us to stand up, like in a line, and we were made to stay awake.

"Your mind starts to play tricks on you. I remember starting to see faces in the wall.

"If we were dozing off or showed any sign that we weren't taking it seriously, things were thrown at us, or we were shouted at, and the punishment was then extended."

He said his older sister tried to protect him.

"Meaghann was effectively like a human mattress," he recalled.

"She took the brunt of sleeping on the concrete, and she would then let myself cuddle into her and rub the back of my head.

"She tried to shield us from as much as possible. She was our protector."

Meaghann said she continued to struggle with feelings of guilt over what happened, as she could not offer more protection.

"I'll live with it for the rest of my life," she said.

"I will never forgive myself for the things I had to see and I couldn't do anything about it.

"I know I was a child, but I didn't see it like that at the time and I still struggle to see it that way."

Rebekah said she has had lifelong mental health problems, has been diagnosed with personality disorder, and has had substance misuse issues.

She described her childhood as "very conflicted".

"There was moments that were happy," she said.

"There's a lot of fond memories amongst all the bad, but the bad outweighs the good.

"There was a lot of laughs, but more often than not there were a lot of tears and a lot of reasons to feel alone."

Police Scotland launched an investigation in 2022 after William made a statement.

The siblings said they decided to speak out in the hope their story may help others.

"I feel like this is the first time we've ever really been given a platform that we can use to make a difference in some way," Meaghann said.

"Even if one person was to take something positive from it, then I've done my bit."

William said he hoped sharing their experiences would help others recognise the signs of abuse.

He concluded: "My mother, grandmother and stepfather are evil, barbaric and cruel.

"But it hasn't changed us. Not in the way they wanted it to anyway."

More stories from North East Scotland, Orkney and Shetland

Listen to news from North East Scotland on BBC Sounds

Solicitor Andrew Ormiston, for Freeman, said she maintained her innocence, and had expressed "confusion" over why the complainers had made the allegations.

John McLeod, for Stephen, said she also continued to maintain her innocence.

Debbie Ginniver, for McColl, said he had admitted the offences, did not seek to justify or excuse his behaviour, and had shown "deep remorse".

Sheriff Findlater told Freeman that "shame has been brought to your name".

He told the three first offenders there were alternative sentences to custody.

Alison McKenzie, procurator fiscal for Grampian, Highlands and Islands, said the trio were adults when they "knowingly and deliberately subjected these children to a horrific catalogue of mistreatment".

She said: "The evidence showed that, rather than providing the care, affection and security every child deserves, they engaged in a sustained pattern of cruelty, degradation and harmful behaviour.

"We hope this prosecution reassures others who have experienced child abuse that they will be listened to, treated with dignity and supported throughout the criminal justice process, regardless of when the offending took place."

Det Insp Kerry McCombie, of Police Scotland, added: "The abuse spanned across the childhood years of the victims and I'd like to pay tribute to them for their bravery to bring this case before the courts."

If you or someone you know have been affected by child abuse, you can find more details of help and support at the BBC Action Line.

title: Vulnerable GOP senator breaks with Trump on 2 key issues as Vance makes stop without her
description: Susan Collins skips JD Vance's Maine visit while opposing Trump's 50% tariffs on Canada and new postal service rules restricting mail-in voting.
fullText:
Sen. Susan Collins of Maine, a moderate Republican seeking re-election in a blue-leaning state, is not joining Vice President JD Vance on Monday as he stops in her home state of Maine.

Collins, who at times has opposed President Donald Trump's legislative priorities, is a top target for Democrats this year as she runs in a midterm race that's among roughly a dozen that will determine if the GOP holds onto its slim Senate majority.

Vance's stop in Maine comes as Collins opposes Trump's move this past weekend to impose 50% tariffs on a range of goods from Canada, which shares a long border with Maine. And the senator is also opposed to new U.S. Postal Service rules that, if implemented, could rein in mail-in voting.

The vice president on Monday delivered remarks in Brewer, Maine, at Compotech, a defense technology manufacturer. It's the second stop this year by Vance in Maine and the second time that Collins has not teamed up with the vice president.

Susan Collins Drops Brutal Reminder Of Democrat Challenger Rocked By Accusations

"I am already scheduled on Monday, so I will not be able to join the vice president," Collins told reporters on Saturday.

The Senate was in session when Vance held an event in Bangor, Maine, in May, and Collins stayed in Washington. The senator holds a historic attendance record of casting over 10,000 consecutive roll call votes in the Senate dating back three decades.

But Collins, speaking to reporters as she marched in the annual Madison-Anson Days parade, her seventh parade this summer, highlighted that she teamed up last week with Energy Secretary Chris Wright when he stopped in Maine to tour a federally funded battery storage project in Lincoln built on the site of a closed paper mill.

"I really appreciated Secretary Wright's presence," Collins said.

What The Latest Fox News Poll In Maine's Crucial Senate Race Shows

Collins, who was one of a small group of Republicans who voted to convict Trump in a 2021 Senate trial after the House impeached him following the Jan. 6 attack on the U.S. Capitol, has at times voted against the Trump administration's wishes.

"I still think imposing new tariffs on Canada is a mistake," Collins said on Saturday.

Collins also referred to the proposed U.S. Post Office rule to implement a Trump executive order to rein in mail-in voting by refusing to deliver absentee ballots in states that have not turned over their raw voter rolls to the Justice Department or Department of Homeland Security.

"Mail-in ballots are very important to the people of Maine," Collins said. "I do not support restrictions that make it more difficult for seniors to cast votes on Election Day via the mail."

Who's Up And Who's Down: Check Out The Fox News Power Rankings On The Midterm Elections

Collins says she supports the House version of the federal SAVE America Act (Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act), which mandates documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote and a photo ID for federal elections. But she joined three other Republicans and all Democrats to vote against advancing a Senate version of the bill, which is a top Trump priority.

Collins has also taken issue with the Trump administration over its crackdown on illegal immigration, and its aggressive deportation efforts. The administration received backlash following the fatal shootings by federal enforcement agents of two U.S. citizens in Minnesota who were protesting immigration operations. And the issue flared again this summer, after a fatal ICE shooting in Biddeford, Maine.

Democrats, including her Senate challenger, former Maine Senate President Troy Jackson, have repeatedly linked her to Trump, and heavily criticized her for her past funding for ICE.

Democracy '26: Stay Up To Date With The Fox News Election Hub

Collins is the only Republican senator running for re-election in a state then-Vice President Kamala Harris carried in the 2024 election. And highlighting her differences with the president and his administration may be beneficial to Collins as she woos independent voters and even some Democrats.

Vance, during his May stop in Maine, said, "Sometimes I get frustrated with Susan Collins."

"I almost wish that she was more partisan. But the thing I love about Susan is she is independent, because Maine is an independent state. And, frankly, if she was as partisan as I sometimes wish that she was, she would not be a good fit for the people of Maine," Vance continued.

Vance added, "Let's give a shoutout to Susan Collins, who's doing a great job."

Jackson's campaign, in a social media post ahead of Vance's visit, called the vice president "Susan's pal."

The vice president reiterated those sentiments in his Monday address in Brewer, Maine, calling Collins his "dear friend."

"As you know, Susan is the most independent member of the United States Senate and, as the president of the United States Senate, she sometimes makes my job a little bit harder. But she makes it harder because she's coming to work every single day and fighting not for a political party… she comes to work every single day and fights for the great people of Maine and I've seen it," Vance said.

Jackson, in a social media post and video ahead of Vance's visit, took aim at Vance and Collins.

"I'm sure JD Vance loves her because she's doing everything that he wants for her, but she's not doing it for Maine people," Jackson argued in an accompanying video.

Vance was joined in Brewer by former two-term Republican Gov. Paul LePage, who is the GOP nominee in Maine's 2nd Congressional District.

The most rural district, the largest in the eastern U.S., is a top flip opportunity for the GOP, with moderate Democratic Rep. Jared Golden declining to seek re-election this year.

title: Clarence Thomas scorches racial litmus tests policing thought: ‘Stay Black and die’
description: Clarence Thomas compared restrictions on Black conservatives' viewpoints to racial segregation in a wide-ranging interview with Sen. Ted Cruz.
fullText:
Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas rejected the idea that Black Americans should be expected to hold particular political views because of their race during a rare interview with Republican Texas Sen. Ted Cruz.

"We had this saying [that there are] only two things I have to do: stay Black and die," Thomas told Cruz, responding to a comment about the conservative justice having an individualist streak. "That was a retort to people who had these sort of requirements for us, these these mandates for us because of our skin color … But at any rate, they think that here's the way you're supposed to think. Again, here's your skin color. There's this kind of deterministic view that you're supposed to think this because we say so."

"And I, of course, declined that invitation. And so now that means that something, that I'm a walking contradiction because I've deviated from their perception of what I should think," the justice added while speaking on the "Verdict with Ted Cruz" podcast.

Democrat Lawmaker Calls Clarence Thomas An 'Uncle Tom' And 'Lynchman' After Supreme Court Redistricting Ruling

Thomas, who is Black, grew up poor in segregated Georgia, initially living in his parents' wooden shack in Pin Point and later in Savannah with his grandparents. As a child, Thomas was raised speaking Gullah, a creole language derived from English spoken by the descendants of African slaves.

At the College of the Holy Cross, he initially embraced left-wing Black nationalism, admired Malcolm X and helped establish the school's Black Student Union. Thomas began moving right after participating in a violent 1970 protest in Cambridge, Massachusetts, later saying his shame over the episode prompted him to reject left-wing activism and reconsider the self-reliance preached by his grandfather.

Clarence Thomas Warns America: Liberty Dies When We Choose Comfort Over Courage

To further explain his point, Thomas compared efforts to dictate which ideas Black Americans should embrace to the restrictions of racial segregation.

"Here's what I've asked people. I said, 'When I was a kid, the Savannah Public Library was segregated.' I said, 'Do you think it was right that the Savannah Public Library was segregated?' Oh, no. You should have been able to go in," Thomas stated. "I said, 'What if they allowed me in but said I couldn't go to certain floors? That would be wrong.' I said, "What about if they said you couldn't go to certain stacks?' Well, that would be wrong. 'What if they had certain books marked that were off limits to me?' That would be wrong."

Black Gop Congressman Shuts Down Race Question Following Supreme Court Redistricting Ruling

"Then my question is, why is it then that you have a problem with me embracing certain ideas in certain books? What's the difference?' Thomas went on.
